car.funFact: Did you know? Modern cars have lights, mirrors, and brakes that help drivers see and stop safely. Electric cars can run with batteries instead of fuel.
car.try: Pretend your hands are on a steering wheel. Turn left, turn right, and say "{name}!"

bus.about: A bus is a big vehicle that carries many people at once. School buses and city buses help families travel together and reduce traffic on roads.
bus.funFact: Did you know? Some buses have special ramps so everyone can get in more easily. In some cities, double-decker buses have two levels of seats.
bus.try: Line up your toys like bus passengers. Say "{name}!" and pretend to ring the stop bell.

taxi.about: A taxi is a car you can hire to go from one place to another. A driver takes you where you ask, and families pay a fare at the end of the ride.
taxi.funFact: Did you know? Taxis can be different colors in different cities. Phone apps can help adults book taxis quickly and safely.
taxi.try: Wave your hand like calling a taxi and say "{name}!" Then politely say, "Please take me home."

policeCar.about: A police car helps police officers protect people and keep roads safe. Officers use police cars to reach places quickly during emergencies.
policeCar.funFact: Did you know? Police cars have flashing lights and sirens so other vehicles know to give way. These signals are only for urgent situations.
policeCar.try: Blink your fingers like flashing lights and say "{name}!" Practice standing safely at the side of a road.

scooter.about: A scooter is a small two-wheel vehicle. Some scooters are kicked by foot, and others have motors. They are useful for short trips in busy areas.
scooter.funFact: Did you know? Helmets protect your head while riding scooters. Riding slowly near people keeps everyone safer.
scooter.try: Take one pretend kick forward and say "{name}!" Then pretend to wear a helmet before riding.

bicycle.about: A bicycle has two wheels, pedals, and handlebars. Children and adults ride bicycles for fun, exercise, and short travel.
bicycle.funFact: Did you know? Bicycles do not need fuel, so they are eco-friendly. Reflectors and lights help riders stay visible.
bicycle.try: Move your legs in the air like pedaling and say "{name}!" Count 1 to 5 like slow pedal turns.

motorcycle.about: A motorcycle is a fast two-wheel motor vehicle. It can move quickly on roads, so riders need balance, attention, and proper safety gear.
motorcycle.funFact: Did you know? Helmets, jackets, and gloves help protect motorcycle riders. Some motorcycles are used by delivery workers and police teams.
motorcycle.try: Pretend to wear a helmet, hold handlebars, and say "{name}!" in a gentle voice.

truck.about: A truck is a strong vehicle that carries heavy goods like food boxes, furniture, and building materials. Trucks help shops and homes get important supplies.
truck.funFact: Did you know? Some trucks have very long trailers for big loads. Delivery trucks bring many of the things we use every day.
truck.try: Pretend to lift a heavy box and load it into a truck. Say "{name}!" and make a soft beep-beep sound.

fireTruck.about: A fire truck carries firefighters, water hoses, and ladders to emergency places. Firefighters use these tools to control fires and help people stay safe.
fireTruck.funFact: Did you know? Fire trucks are usually bright red so people can spot them quickly. Their ladders can reach high floors of buildings.
fireTruck.try: Say "{name}!" and pretend to hold a hose with both hands. Then practice a quiet siren sound.

ambulance.about: An ambulance is an emergency vehicle that takes sick or injured people to hospitals quickly. Medical helpers inside give first aid while traveling.
ambulance.funFact: Did you know? Ambulances use lights and sirens to move through traffic faster. Other vehicles should make space when an ambulance passes.
ambulance.try: Put one hand on your heart, take a calm breath, and say "{name}!" Then say, "Please make way."

train.about: A train runs on metal tracks and can carry many people or goods in connected coaches. Trains are useful for long-distance and city travel.
train.funFact: Did you know? Some trains are very fast, while others carry heavy cargo. Train stations help people move safely from one city to another.
train.try: Move your arms like train rods and say "{name}!" Count how many imaginary coaches your train has.

metro.about: A metro is a city train, often underground or on raised tracks. Metros help people avoid road traffic and reach places on time.
metro.funFact: Did you know? Metro trains stop at many stations, and doors open automatically. Many people use metros daily for school and work.
metro.try: Stand still and pretend to hold a metro pole. Sway gently and say "{name}!"

tractor.about: A tractor is a powerful farm vehicle used to plow fields and pull tools. Farmers use tractors to prepare land and grow crops we eat.
tractor.funFact: Did you know? Tractors move slowly but can pull very heavy equipment. Different tractor tools help with sowing, watering, and harvesting.
tractor.try: Walk slowly with strong steps like a tractor and say "{name}!"

airplane.about: An airplane flies high in the sky using wings and engines. Airplanes help people travel between faraway cities and countries much faster than roads.
airplane.funFact: Did you know? Pilots and cabin crew train carefully for safe flights. Airplanes can fly above clouds where the sky looks bright and wide.
airplane.try: Spread your arms like wings, glide in place, and say "{name}!"

helicopter.about: A helicopter has spinning blades on top that let it lift straight up and hover. Helicopters can land in small places where big planes cannot.
helicopter.funFact: Did you know? Helicopters help in rescue missions, medical transport, and news reporting. Their spinning rotors create the loud chop-chop sound.
helicopter.try: Spin one finger above your head like a rotor and say "{name}!" softly.

rocket.about: A rocket is a powerful vehicle that travels into space. Rockets carry satellites, science tools, and sometimes astronauts beyond Earth.
rocket.funFact: Did you know? Rockets need huge force to escape Earth's gravity. Space missions help us learn about planets, weather, and stars.
rocket.try: Count down with a grown-up: 3, 2, 1... Say "{name}!" and do one careful jump.

boat.about: A boat is a water vehicle that floats on rivers, lakes, or near the shore. Some boats use oars, while others use sails or motors.
boat.funFact: Did you know? Boats float because their shape pushes water aside. Life jackets are important safety gear when riding boats.
boat.try: Sit and rock gently side to side like small waves, then say "{name}!"

ship.about: A ship is a very large water vehicle built for seas and oceans. Ships carry passengers, cars, food, and containers across long distances.
ship.funFact: Did you know? Cargo ships move many products between countries. Some ships are taller than buildings and have giant engines.
ship.try: Wave like a sailor and say "{name}!" Then pretend to spot land with your hand above your eyes.

a.description: A is for Apple, a sweet and crunchy fruit that grows on trees!
a.funFact: Apples come in many colors: red, green, and yellow!

b.description: B is for Ball, round and bouncy, perfect for playing!
b.funFact: Balls can bounce high when you throw them down!

c.description: C is for Cat, a soft and furry friend with whiskers!

d.description: D is for Dog, a loyal and friendly pet that loves to play!

e.description: E is for Elephant, the biggest land animal with a long trunk!

f.description: F is for Fish, colorful swimmers that live underwater!
f.funFact: Fish breathe through gills and can swim very fast!

g.description: G is for Gun, a tool used by police or soldiers, and it is not a toy.
g.funFact: Real guns can be dangerous, so children should never touch them.

h.description: H is for House, a cozy place where families live together!
h.funFact: Every house is special and different, just like you!

i.description: I is for Ice Cream, a cold and sweet treat on a hot day!
i.funFact: Ice cream comes in so many yummy flavors!

j.description: J is for Jug, a container used to pour water, milk, or juice!

k.description: K is for Kite, flying high in the sky on a windy day!
k.funFact: Kites need wind to fly up into the sky!

l.description: L is for Lion, the brave king of the jungle with a big mane!
l.funFact: Lions live in groups called prides!

m.description: M is for Monkey, swinging through trees and eating bananas!
m.funFact: Monkeys love to play and are very good climbers!

n.description: N is for Nest, a cozy home where birds lay their eggs!
n.funFact: Birds build nests with twigs and leaves!

o.description: O is for Orange, a juicy fruit full of vitamin C!
o.funFact: Oranges are both a fruit and a color!

p.description: P is for Parrot, a colorful bird with a curved beak!
p.funFact: Parrots can copy sounds and even learn to say simple words!

q.description: Q is for Queen, a royal leader who wears a beautiful crown!
q.funFact: Queens live in palaces and wear fancy dresses!

r.description: R is for Rabbit, a soft and cute animal with long ears!
r.funFact: Rabbits can hop quickly and love to nibble carrots and leafy greens!

s.description: S is for Sun, shining bright and keeping us warm every day!
s.funFact: The sun is a big star that gives us light and warmth!

t.description: T is for Tiger, a big wild cat with bright stripes!
t.funFact: Every tiger has a unique stripe pattern, just like a fingerprint!

u.description: U is for Umbrella, keeping us dry when it rains!
u.funFact: Umbrellas come in many colors and patterns!

v.description: V is for Violin, a musical instrument that makes beautiful sounds!
v.funFact: You play the violin with a bow and make lovely music!

w.description: W is for Watch, a handy clock you wear on your wrist!
w.funFact: A watch helps us know the time for school, play, and sleep!

x.description: X is for Xmas Tree, a decorated tree used at Christmas time!
x.funFact: People decorate Xmas trees with lights, stars, and colorful ornaments!

y.description: Y is for Yak, a strong and furry animal that lives in cold mountains!
y.funFact: Yaks have thick coats that keep them warm in snowy weather!

z.description: Z is for Zebra, a striped animal that looks like a horse!
z.funFact: Every zebra has its own unique stripe pattern!

indianFestivals.title: Indian Festivals
indianFestivals.description: Explore 95 festivals of India — tap any card to hear its name and learn fun facts.
indianFestivals.tapAgain: Close this box and tap the same card to hear the festival name again.

dialog.hint: Look at the picture and say: {name}!

republicDay.about: Republic Day is celebrated on 26 January every year. On this day in 1950, India became a republic with its own Constitution — a big book of rules that helps everyone live fairly and safely. Schools hold flag ceremonies, parades, and patriotic songs.
republicDay.funFact: Did you know? A grand Republic Day parade happens in New Delhi with marching soldiers, colorful floats, and dances from different states!
republicDay.try: Stand tall like a soldier, salute gently, and say "{name}!" Draw the tricolor flag with saffron, white, and green stripes.

independenceDay.about: Independence Day is celebrated on 15 August. It marks the day India became free in 1947. People hoist the national flag, sing patriotic songs, and remember the brave freedom fighters who worked hard for our country.
independenceDay.funFact: Did you know? The Prime Minister hoists the flag at the Red Fort in Delhi every Independence Day while kites fly across India!
independenceDay.try: Wave your hand like a flag in the wind and say "{name}!" Tell one thing you love about India.

gandhiJayanti.about: Gandhi Jayanti on 2 October celebrates the birthday of Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation. He taught peace, truth, and non-violence. On this day, people remember to speak kindly, help others, and keep surroundings clean.
gandhiJayanti.funFact: Did you know? Gandhi ji used simple clothes and walked long distances to spread his message of peace and unity!
gandhiJayanti.try: Walk slowly and quietly for ten steps. Say "{name}!" and pick up one piece of paper to keep your room clean.

childrensDay.about: Children's Day is celebrated on 14 November in India — the birthday of Jawaharlal Nehru, who loved children and called them the future of the nation. Schools hold fun programs, games, sweets, and special activities just for kids.
childrensDay.funFact: Did you know? Nehru ji was often called Chacha Nehru because he cared so much for children!
childrensDay.try: Smile big and say "{name}!" Tell a grown-up one dream you have for when you grow up.

teachersDay.about: Teachers' Day is celebrated on 5 September — the birthday of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, a great teacher and former President of India. Students thank teachers with cards, flowers, and songs.
teachersDay.funFact: Did you know? Dr. Radhakrishnan asked that his birthday be celebrated as Teachers' Day instead of a personal holiday!
teachersDay.try: Say "{name}!" and thank one teacher for something they taught you.

constitutionDay.about: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) on 26 November remembers the day India adopted its Constitution in 1949. Schools read about fundamental rights, duties, and how laws keep citizens equal and free.
constitutionDay.funFact: Did you know? Dr. B. R. Ambedkar is called the chief architect of the Indian Constitution!
constitutionDay.try: Say "{name}!" and name one good rule that helps everyone at home or school.

nationalYouthDay.about: National Youth Day on 12 January celebrates the birthday of Swami Vivekananda, who inspired young people to be brave, kind, and strong in mind and body.
nationalYouthDay.funFact: Did you know? Swami Vivekananda gave a famous speech in Chicago that made the world admire Indian wisdom!
nationalYouthDay.try: Stand tall, stretch your arms like a sunrise, and say "{name}!" Share one brave goal for yourself.

nationalUnityDay.about: National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) on 31 October honors Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who helped unite many states into one India. People take a pledge of unity and togetherness.
nationalUnityDay.funFact: Did you know? Patel is called the Iron Man of India for bringing the country's states together!
nationalUnityDay.try: Hold a friend's hand gently and say "{name}!" Tell why friends and neighbors matter.

internationalWomensDay.about: International Women's Day on 8 March celebrates the strength, kindness, and achievements of girls and women everywhere. Schools and homes thank mothers, sisters, teachers, and leaders.
internationalWomensDay.funFact: Did you know? The color purple is often used on this day to show respect and equality for women!
internationalWomensDay.try: Say "{name}!" and thank one woman who helps you every day.

worldEnvironmentDay.about: World Environment Day on 5 June teaches us to care for Earth — trees, rivers, animals, and clean air. Families plant saplings, save water, and reduce plastic waste.
worldEnvironmentDay.funFact: Did you know? Planting just one tree can give shade, fruit, and homes for birds for many years!
worldEnvironmentDay.try: Water a plant or pretend to plant a seed. Say "{name}!" and name one way you can help Earth.

internationalYogaDay.about: International Yoga Day on 21 June celebrates yoga — gentle body stretches and calm breathing that India shared with the world. Kids learn simple poses for health and focus.
internationalYogaDay.funFact: Did you know? The United Nations chose 21 June because it is among the longest days of the year in the Northern Hemisphere!
internationalYogaDay.try: Sit tall, breathe in slowly three times, and say "{name}!" Try a soft mountain pose with arms up.

nationalDoctorsDay.about: National Doctors' Day on 1 July thanks doctors and healthcare heroes who help sick people feel better. It reminds children that medicine, kindness, and care save lives.
nationalDoctorsDay.funFact: Did you know? In India this day honors Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy, a famous doctor and leader!
nationalDoctorsDay.try: Pretend to check a teddy's heartbeat gently. Say "{name}!" and thank doctors who keep us healthy.

worldAnimalDay.about: World Animal Day on 4 October celebrates kindness to animals — pets, birds, and wild creatures. Children learn to feed, care, and never hurt living beings.
worldAnimalDay.funFact: Did you know? Being gentle with animals is called compassion — a word India also teaches as ahimsa!
worldAnimalDay.try: Pat your pet or hug a soft toy carefully. Say "{name}!" and name one animal you love.

nationalMathematicsDay.about: National Mathematics Day on 22 December celebrates the birthday of great mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan. Schools play number games and discover how maths is fun and magical.
nationalMathematicsDay.funFact: Did you know? Ramanujan found amazing number patterns even with very little paper when he was young!
nationalMathematicsDay.try: Clap and count to ten. Say "{name}!" and solve one tiny sum with a smile.

nationalFarmersDay.about: National Farmers' Day (Kisan Diwas) on 23 December thanks farmers who grow our food — rice, wheat, fruits, and vegetables. Without farmers, our plates would be empty.
nationalFarmersDay.funFact: Did you know? Chaudhary Charan Singh's birthday is remembered as Kisan Diwas because he worked for farmers!
nationalFarmersDay.try: Pretend to sow seeds in the soil. Say "{name}!" and thank a farmer for your food.

unitedNationsDay.about: United Nations Day on 24 October remembers the UN, which works for peace, children's rights, and help across countries. India is a proud member that believes in world friendship.
unitedNationsDay.funFact: Did you know? The UN blue flag with a world map reminds everyone that we share one planet!
unitedNationsDay.try: Shake hands with a friend and say "{name}!" Wish peace for every country.

nationalSportsDay.about: National Sports Day on 29 August honors Major Dhyan Chand, a hockey legend. Schools organize races, games, and fitness activities to celebrate sportsmanship.
nationalSportsDay.funFact: Did you know? Dhyan Chand was so skilled that fans called him the Wizard of Hockey!
nationalSportsDay.try: Run in place for ten seconds. Say "{name}!" and cheer for your favorite sport.

diwali.about: Diwali is the Festival of Lights, usually in October or November. Families clean homes, light diyas, draw rangoli, wear new clothes, share sweets, and pray for happiness. It celebrates light winning over darkness and good over evil.
diwali.funFact: Did you know? Different parts of India tell different Diwali stories — like Lord Rama returning home or Goddess Lakshmi bringing good fortune!
diwali.try: Cup your hands like holding a glowing diya. Say "{name}!" and draw a tiny rangoli with chalk.

dhanteras.about: Dhanteras comes two days before Diwali. Families buy utensils, lamps, or small gold and pray to Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Dhanvantari for health and prosperity.
dhanteras.funFact: Did you know? Dhanvantari is remembered as the divine doctor of Ayurveda!
dhanteras.try: Polish an imaginary coin until it shines. Say "{name}!" and wish health for your family.

govardhanPuja.about: Govardhan Puja (Annakut) is celebrated a day after Diwali. Devotees remember Lord Krishna lifting Govardhan Hill to protect villagers and offer mountains of delicious food.
govardhanPuja.funFact: Did you know? Annakut means a mountain of food — temples and homes display many dishes!
govardhanPuja.try: Build a tiny hill with pillows. Say "{name}!" and thank nature for food and shelter.

bhaiDooj.about: Bhai Dooj comes after Diwali. Sisters apply a tilak on brothers' foreheads, pray for their long life, and brothers give gifts. It celebrates loving sibling bonds.
bhaiDooj.funFact: Did you know? Similar brother-sister days are celebrated as Bhai Tika in Nepal!
bhaiDooj.try: Gently pretend to put a tilak. Say "{name}!" and share one kind wish with a sibling or friend.

holi.about: Holi is the Festival of Colors, celebrated in spring (usually March). People play with safe colored powders and water, dance, sing, and forgive old quarrels. It welcomes spring and friendship.
holi.funFact: Did you know? The night before Holi many families light Holika Dahan, remembering good winning over evil!
holi.try: Spin gently and pretend colors fly — pink, yellow, green! Say "{name}!" and laugh with someone you love.

holikaDahan.about: Holika Dahan is the bonfire night before Holi. Communities gather around a sacred fire to remember the story of Prahlad and Holika, where devotion and goodness win.
holikaDahan.funFact: Did you know? Roasting corn or sweets near the Holika fire is a fun tradition in many towns!
holikaDahan.try: Warm your hands near an imaginary fire. Say "{name}!" and whisper one good wish.

dussehra.about: Dussehra (Vijayadashami) marks the victory of good over evil at the end of Navratri. Ramlila plays show Lord Rama defeating Ravana, and giant Ravana effigies are burned in many places.
dussehra.funFact: Did you know? Mysuru's Dussehra procession with decorated elephants is famous across India!
dussehra.try: Pretend to shoot an arrow like Rama — whoosh! Say "{name}!" and cheer for good winning over bad.

navratri.about: Navratri means nine nights of devotion to Goddess Durga. In Gujarat people play garba and dandiya; in other states people fast, pray, and celebrate courage. The tenth day is Dussehra.
navratri.funFact: Did you know? Each of the nine nights honors a different form of the Goddess!
navratri.try: Clap-clap and spin one slow turn like garba. Say "{name}!" and wear an imaginary bright dupatta.

durgaPuja.about: Durga Puja is a grand festival in West Bengal and eastern India celebrating Goddess Durga's victory. Beautiful pandals are built, idols are worshipped for days, and then immersed with drums and joy.
durgaPuja.funFact: Did you know? Kolkata's Durga Puja pandals can look like magical art galleries!
durgaPuja.try: Beat an imaginary dhak drum — dhaak dhaak! Say "{name}!" and bow respectfully.

ganeshChaturthi.about: Ganesh Chaturthi celebrates Lord Ganesha, the elephant-headed god of wisdom and new beginnings. Families bring home idols, offer modak sweets, sing aarti, and later immerse idols with love.
ganeshChaturthi.funFact: Did you know? Mumbai's Ganesh celebrations are among the biggest in the world!
ganeshChaturthi.try: Make Ganesha ears with your hands on your head. Say "{name}!" and pretend to eat one sweet modak.

janmashtami.about: Janmashtami (Krishna Janmashtami) celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna. At midnight people sing bhajans, swing baby Krishna's cradle, and children enjoy dahi handi pyramids in many cities.
janmashtami.funFact: Did you know? Stories call Krishna Makhan Chor — the butter thief — because he loved butter so much!
janmashtami.try: Pretend to steal butter sneakily and giggle. Say "{name}!" and clap for a dahi handi team.

ramNavami.about: Ram Navami celebrates the birth of Lord Rama, the hero of the Ramayana. Temples hold readings, bhajans, and processions with tiny idols of baby Rama.
ramNavami.funFact: Did you know? Ayodhya, Rama's birthplace, holds grand Ram Navami celebrations with lamps!
ramNavami.try: Bow gently like a cradle story. Say "{name}!" and name one good deed Rama did.

mahaShivaratri.about: Maha Shivaratri is the Great Night of Lord Shiva, celebrated with fasting, temple visits, and night prayers. Devotees offer milk, bilva leaves, and flowers.
mahaShivaratri.funFact: Did you know? Many devotees stay awake all night singing Shiva bhajans!
mahaShivaratri.try: Fold your hands quietly and say "Om Namah Shivaya." Say "{name}!" with a calm voice.

hanumanJayanti.about: Hanuman Jayanti celebrates Lord Hanuman, the brave monkey god of strength, loyalty, and courage. Devotees visit temples, chant Hanuman Chalisa, and offer red flowers and laddus.
hanumanJayanti.funFact: Did you know? Hanuman could leap across the ocean to help Rama — a story of courage and devotion!
hanumanJayanti.try: Flex your arms like a superhero. Say "{name}!" and do one brave kind act today.

basantPanchami.about: Vasant Panchami (Basant Panchami) marks spring and honors Goddess Saraswati of learning, music, and art. People wear yellow, fly kites, and pray for wisdom.
basantPanchami.funFact: Did you know? Mustard flowers bloom bright yellow in spring — that is why yellow is special on this day!
basantPanchami.try: Point to something yellow. Say "{name}!" and hum one song you know.

akshayaTritiya.about: Akshaya Tritiya is considered a day of never-ending good luck. Families start new projects, buy gold, plant trees, and do charity — believing good deeds grow forever.
akshayaTritiya.funFact: Did you know? "Akshaya" means something that never finishes — like kindness that keeps growing!
akshayaTritiya.try: Start a tiny good habit — share a smile. Say "{name}!" and plant one imaginary seed of kindness.

rakshaBandhan.about: Raksha Bandhan celebrates the loving bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters tie a colorful rakhi, brothers promise to care, and families share sweets together.
rakshaBandhan.funFact: Did you know? Friends and cousins also tie rakhis to show love and protection!
rakshaBandhan.try: Pretend to tie a rakhi gently. Say "{name}!" and make one kind promise.

karvaChauth.about: Karwa Chauth is a festival of love and togetherness when many married women fast until moonrise and pray for their family's well-being. Families then share a special meal.
karvaChauth.funFact: Did you know? Looking at the moon through a sieve (chalni) is a popular Karwa Chauth tradition!
karvaChauth.try: Wave softly at the moon. Say "{name}!" and wish your family well.

chhathPuja.about: Chhath Puja is a four-day festival in Bihar, Jharkhand, and eastern UP dedicated to the Sun God. Devotees offer prayers at sunrise and sunset standing in rivers or ponds.
chhathPuja.funFact: Did you know? Chhath Puja is eco-friendly — offerings are made in nature without idols!
chhathPuja.try: Stretch your arms toward an imaginary sunrise. Say "{name}!" and thank the sun.

guruPurnima.about: Guru Purnima honors teachers and gurus who guide us with knowledge. Students thank teachers, and ashrams hold special prayers on this full-moon day.
guruPurnima.funFact: Did you know? Hindus, Buddhists, and Jains all honor teachers on Guru Purnima!
guruPurnima.try: Fold your hands and thank someone who teaches you. Say "{name}!"

rathYatra.about: Rath Yatra is the famous chariot festival of Lord Jagannath in Puri, Odisha. Huge wooden chariots carry the deities through the streets while millions of devotees pull the ropes.
rathYatra.funFact: Did you know? The English word "juggernaut" comes from Jagannath's giant chariot!
rathYatra.try: Pretend to pull a chariot rope with friends. Say "{name}!" and cheer loudly.

kumbhMela.about: Kumbh Mela is one of the world's largest peaceful gatherings. Pilgrims bathe at holy rivers in Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik, or Ujjain to seek purity and blessings.
kumbhMela.funFact: Did you know? Millions of people come together at Kumbh Mela — making it a wonder of faith and togetherness!
kumbhMela.try: Walk calmly in a quiet line. Say "{name}!" and imagine a river sparkling with lamps.

tulsiVivah.about: Tulsi Vivah celebrates the ceremonial wedding of the sacred tulsi plant with Lord Vishnu (or Shaligram). Homes decorate the tulsi and mark the start of the wedding season.
tulsiVivah.funFact: Did you know? Tulsi is loved as a healing plant — many Indian courtyards grow it with care!
tulsiVivah.try: Water a plant gently. Say "{name}!" and thank green plants for fresh air.

nagPanchami.about: Nag Panchami honors snakes as guardians of nature. People draw nag motifs, offer milk or flowers near snake homes or images, and learn respect for wildlife.
nagPanchami.funFact: Did you know? Snakes help farmers by eating mice and pests in fields!
nagPanchami.try: Draw a friendly curly snake in the air. Say "{name}!" and promise to respect animals.

ahoiAshtami.about: Ahoi Ashtami is a festival where mothers keep a fast and pray for their children's long life and happiness. Stories of Ahoi Mata are told with love and care.
ahoiAshtami.funFact: Did you know? Many mothers draw Ahoi Mata and animals on a wall as part of the ritual!
ahoiAshtami.try: Give your mother or caregiver a hug. Say "{name}!" and thank them for caring for you.

vatPurnima.about: Vat Purnima is celebrated mainly in Maharashtra and Gujarat. Married women tie threads around a banyan (vat) tree and pray for family happiness.
vatPurnima.funFact: Did you know? The banyan tree is one of India's most sacred trees and can live for hundreds of years!
vatPurnima.try: Hug a tree carefully (or pretend). Say "{name}!" and thank trees for shade.

teej.about: Hariyali Teej welcomes green monsoon beauty. Women wear green clothes, swing on jhulas, sing folk songs, and celebrate love and nature after the rains begin.
teej.funFact: Did you know? "Hariyali" means greenery — Teej is all about lush green leaves and happy swings!
teej.try: Pretend to swing on a jhula. Say "{name}!" and name something green outside.

gangaur.about: Gangaur is a colorful Rajasthan festival honoring Goddess Gauri (Parvati) and Lord Shiva. Women dress in bright clothes, carry beautiful statues, and celebrate marital bliss and spring.
gangaur.funFact: Did you know? Gangaur processions in Jaipur are famous for music, colors, and royal cheer!
gangaur.try: Walk proudly like a festival procession. Say "{name}!" and clap to a rhythm.

vivahaPanchami.about: Vivaha Panchami remembers the sacred wedding of Lord Rama and Sita. Temples in Ayodhya and Janakpur hold wedding-like celebrations with music and joy.
vivahaPanchami.funFact: Did you know? Janakpur (in Nepal) is linked with Sita's childhood home in these stories!
vivahaPanchami.try: Ring imaginary wedding bells softly. Say "{name}!" and smile a wedding smile.

makarSankranti.about: Makar Sankranti marks the sun's journey into Capricorn and longer days. People fly colorful kites, eat til-gud sweets, and thank the sun for warmth and harvest.
makarSankranti.funFact: Did you know? Gujarat's International Kite Festival fills the sky with thousands of bright kites!
makarSankranti.try: Run slowly with arms spread like a kite. Say "{name}!" and pretend your kite soars — wheee!

pongal.about: Pongal is a four-day harvest festival in Tamil Nadu, usually in January. Families cook sweet Pongal rice, decorate cows, draw kolam, and thank the sun, rain, and farmers.
pongal.funFact: Did you know? "Pongal" means to boil over — a sign of abundance and joy!
pongal.try: Stir an imaginary pot and say "Pongalo Pongal!" Then say "{name}!"

lohri.about: Lohri is a winter festival in Punjab and North India on 13 January with bonfires, popcorn, rewri sweets, and bhangra dance. It welcomes longer sunshine.
lohri.funFact: Did you know? People toss popcorn and peanuts into the Lohri fire while singing folk songs!
lohri.try: Pretend to toss popcorn into a warm fire. Say "{name}!" and do one bhangra clap.

baisakhi.about: Baisakhi (Vaisakhi) is Punjab's harvest festival in April. Farmers thank God for the wheat crop. For Sikhs it also marks the founding of the Khalsa. Bhangra fills the celebrations!
baisakhi.funFact: Did you know? Guru Gobind Singh ji founded the Khalsa on Baisakhi in 1699!
baisakhi.try: Do two bhangra steps — bounce and clap! Say "{name}!" and thank a farmer.

onam.about: Onam is Kerala's harvest festival with flower carpets (pookalam), boat races, Onam sadya feasts on banana leaves, and dances welcoming King Mahabali.
onam.funFact: Did you know? An Onam sadya can have more than 20 dishes on one banana leaf!
onam.try: Arrange imaginary flowers in a circle. Say "{name}!" and pretend one tasty sadya bite.

bihu.about: Bihu is Assam's harvest festival celebrated three times a year — Rongali (spring), Bhogali (winter harvest), and Kongali (autumn). People dance Bihu, sing folk songs, and eat pitha.
bihu.funFact: Did you know? Rongali Bihu also welcomes the Assamese New Year with drums and joy!
bihu.try: Tap your feet quickly — dhol dhol! Say "{name}!" and sway like a Bihu dancer.

nuakhai.about: Nuakhai means "eating the new rice." Families in Odisha celebrate the first harvest with prayers, new clothes, and sharing freshly cooked rice together.
nuakhai.funFact: Did you know? Elders give blessings first, then the whole family tastes the new harvest!
nuakhai.try: Offer an imaginary bowl of rice with respect. Say "{name}!" and thank the fields.

nabanna.about: Nabanna is Bengal's harvest festival that celebrates new rice and rural culture with folk songs, dances, and community feasts.
nabanna.funFact: Did you know? "Nabanna" literally means new rice — a joyful thank-you to the harvest!
nabanna.try: Clap a folk rhythm. Say "{name}!" and thank farmers for rice.

ugadi.about: Ugadi is the New Year in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka. People eat ugadi pachadi with six tastes to remember that life has many flavors.
ugadi.funFact: Did you know? The six tastes of ugadi pachadi teach that life has happy and hard moments — and we accept all!
ugadi.try: Make six fun faces — sweet, sour, salty! Say "{name}!" and welcome a new year.

gudiPadwa.about: Gudi Padwa is the Maharashtrian New Year. Families raise a bright gudi flag, clean homes, eat puran poli, and welcome fresh beginnings.
gudiPadwa.funFact: Did you know? The gudi uses bright cloth, mango leaves, and a sugar flower on bamboo!
gudiPadwa.try: Wave your hand like a bright flag. Say "{name}!" and wish a happy new year.

vishu.about: Vishu is the Malayalam New Year in Kerala. Families prepare Vishu kani — flowers, fruits, rice, gold, and a mirror seen first in the morning for good luck.
vishu.funFact: Did you know? Children receive Vishukkaineetam gift money from elders on Vishu!
vishu.try: Cover your eyes, open them, and say "{name}!" Look at something beautiful first.

puthandu.about: Puthandu is the Tamil New Year, usually in mid-April. Families draw kolam, prepare mango pachadi, visit temples, and wish each other a happy new year.
puthandu.funFact: Did you know? Mango pachadi on Puthandu mixes sweet, sour, and bitter — just like life's flavors!
puthandu.try: Draw dots for a kolam. Say "{name}!" and wish someone a sweet new year.

pohelaBoishakh.about: Pohela Boishakh is the Bengali New Year. People wear colorful clothes, enjoy processions, sweets, and shout "Shubho Noboborsho!" for a happy new year.
pohelaBoishakh.funFact: Did you know? Mangal Shobhajatra is a joyful New Year procession recognized by UNESCO!
pohelaBoishakh.try: Wave and say "Shubho Noboborsho!" Then say "{name}!" with a big smile.

chetiChand.about: Cheti Chand is the Sindhi New Year celebrating the birth of Jhulelal. Communities hold processions, bhajans, and cultural programs with pride.
chetiChand.funFact: Did you know? Jhulelal is remembered as the patron saint of Sindhi people!
chetiChand.try: Clap to a celebratory beat. Say "{name}!" and wish happiness to your community.

bathukamma.about: Bathukamma is Telangana's flower festival where women stack colorful flowers into beautiful conical arrangements and sing while dancing around them.
bathukamma.funFact: Did you know? "Bathukamma" means Mother Goddess come alive — flowers celebrate women and nature!
bathukamma.try: Stack imaginary flower circles. Say "{name}!" and dance one soft circle step.

bonalu.about: Bonalu is a Hyderabad–Telangana festival where devotees offer bonam (rice, milk, jaggery) to Goddess Mahakali in decorated pots with neem leaves.
bonalu.funFact: Did you know? Bonalu processions include drums, dances, and brightly dressed devotees!
bonalu.try: Carry an imaginary pot carefully on your head. Say "{name}!" and walk proudly.

karmaFestival.about: Karma Festival is celebrated by tribal communities in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and nearby regions. People dance around the Karma tree and thank nature for crops.
karmaFestival.funFact: Did you know? The Karma dance can go on all night with flutes and drums!
karmaFestival.try: Dance in a happy circle. Say "{name}!" and thank trees and crops.

eidUlFitr.about: Eid-ul-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan. Muslim families wear new clothes, pray at mosques, share sevaiyan sweets, give gifts, and visit friends and relatives.
eidUlFitr.funFact: Did you know? Zakat-ul-Fitr charity is given so that every family can enjoy Eid with food!
eidUlFitr.try: Say "{name}!" and wish a friend "Eid Mubarak!" Draw a crescent moon in the air.

eidUlAdha.about: Eid-ul-Adha (Bakrid) honors Prophet Ibrahim's devotion. Families pray, share food with neighbors, and help those in need.
eidUlAdha.funFact: Did you know? Sharing meat and meals with the poor is a core message of Eid-ul-Adha!
eidUlAdha.try: Say "{name}!" and share an imaginary treat with someone. Wish "Eid Mubarak!"

ramadan.about: Ramadan (Ramzan) is the holy month when Muslims fast from dawn to sunset, pray, and read the Quran. It teaches patience, gratitude, and caring for the hungry.
ramadan.funFact: Did you know? Iftar is the evening meal that breaks the fast — often starting with dates and water!
ramadan.try: Say "{name}!" and think of one kind thing you can do for someone today.

muharram.about: Muharram is the first month of the Islamic calendar and a time of reflection. Ashura remembers important historical events with prayers and remembrance.
muharram.funFact: Did you know? Muharram teaches bravery, truth, and standing up for what is right!
muharram.try: Walk slowly and quietly. Say "{name}!" and think about being kind and fair.

miladUnNabi.about: Milad-un-Nabi (Eid-e-Milad) celebrates the birthday of Prophet Muhammad. Communities organize prayers, processions, sermons about kindness, and charity.
miladUnNabi.funFact: Did you know? Many Milad gatherings teach children about honesty, mercy, and helping others!
miladUnNabi.try: Speak one kind sentence. Say "{name}!" and smile gently.

shabEBarat.about: Shab-e-Barat is a night of prayer and seeking forgiveness. People visit graves of loved ones, pray for peace, and ask for a good year ahead.
shabEBarat.funFact: Did you know? Many families light lamps and stay up late in prayer on this night!
shabEBarat.try: Sit quietly and make one peaceful wish. Say "{name}!" softly.

shabEQadr.about: Shab-e-Qadr is one of the holiest nights in Ramadan. Muslims pray, read the Quran, and believe this night is full of blessings and mercy.
shabEQadr.funFact: Did you know? Many people stay awake almost the whole night of Shab-e-Qadr in prayer!
shabEQadr.try: Fold your hands and take three calm breaths. Say "{name}!" with respect.

guruNanakJayanti.about: Guru Nanak Jayanti (Gurpurab) celebrates Guru Nanak Dev ji, founder of Sikhism. Sikhs visit gurdwaras, sing shabads, join nagar kirtan, and serve langar — free food for everyone.
guruNanakJayanti.funFact: Did you know? In langar, rich or poor, everyone sits together and eats as equals!
guruNanakJayanti.try: Fold your hands and say "{name}!" Share an imaginary roti with a friend.

holaMohalla.about: Hola Mohalla is a Sikh festival of martial arts, horsemanship, poetry, and music, especially at Anandpur Sahib. It celebrates bravery and community spirit after Holi.
holaMohalla.funFact: Did you know? Mock battles and gatka (martial arts) shows thrill thousands of visitors!
holaMohalla.try: Strike a brave pose like a warrior. Say "{name}!" and cheer for courage.

guruGobindSinghJayanti.about: Guru Gobind Singh Jayanti celebrates the tenth Sikh Guru who created the Khalsa and taught courage, equality, and standing against injustice.
guruGobindSinghJayanti.funFact: Did you know? Guru Gobind Singh ji also composed beautiful poetry and hymns!
guruGobindSinghJayanti.try: Stand brave and kind. Say "{name}!" and name one fair rule you follow.

maghi.about: Maghi is observed a day after Lohri. Sikhs remember the bravery of the forty liberated ones (Chaar Sahibzaade related history of martyrs at Muktsar) and gather for prayers and langar.
maghi.funFact: Did you know? Muktsar Sahib hosts a big Maghi fair with devotion and community meals!
maghi.try: Say "{name}!" with respect and thank brave helpers who protect others.

bandiChhorDivas.about: Bandi Chhor Divas celebrates Guru Hargobind Sahib ji freeing himself and 52 princes from captivity. Gurdwaras are lit beautifully, often around the Diwali season.
bandiChhorDivas.funFact: Did you know? "Bandi Chhor" means liberator of prisoners — a story of justice and freedom!
bandiChhorDivas.try: Open your hands like freeing birds. Say "{name}!" and wish freedom and fairness.

christmas.about: Christmas on 25 December celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ. Christian families attend church, decorate trees, sing carols, exchange gifts, and share cake.
christmas.funFact: Did you know? Goa, Kerala, and Northeast India have beautiful Christmas midnight masses!
christmas.try: Sing "Jingle bells" softly. Say "{name}!" and draw a star on an imaginary tree.

goodFriday.about: Good Friday remembers the crucifixion of Jesus Christ. Churches hold solemn prayers about love, sacrifice, and forgiveness.
goodFriday.funFact: Did you know? Good Friday is followed by Easter Sunday — a day of hope and new life!
goodFriday.try: Sit quietly for ten seconds. Say "{name}!" and think of one kind act.

easter.about: Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ. Families attend church, decorate eggs, and share joyful meals.
easter.funFact: Did you know? Easter egg hunts are fun games where children search for colorful eggs!
easter.try: Pretend to find a hidden egg — peek, peek! Say "{name}!" and hop happily.

palmSunday.about: Palm Sunday marks Jesus's joyful entry into Jerusalem. Churches distribute palm leaves, and children wave them during hymns.
palmSunday.funFact: Did you know? Palm Sunday begins Holy Week leading to Good Friday and Easter!
palmSunday.try: Wave a paper leaf or your hand like a palm. Say "{name}!" and cheer gently.

newYear.about: New Year on 1 January welcomes a fresh calendar year. Families in India celebrate with parties, resolutions, fireworks, and hopes for health and happiness.
newYear.funFact: Did you know? Many people write new year goals — like reading more or being kinder!
newYear.try: Count down 3-2-1! Say "{name}!" and name one happy wish for the year.

ascensionDay.about: Ascension Day remembers Jesus ascending to heaven after Easter. Churches hold special prayers about hope and faith.
ascensionDay.funFact: Did you know? Ascension Day comes forty days after Easter in the Christian calendar!
ascensionDay.try: Look up at the sky calmly. Say "{name}!" and make a peaceful wish.

pentecost.about: Pentecost celebrates the coming of the Holy Spirit to the disciples. Churches often use the color red and sing joyful hymns.
pentecost.funFact: Did you know? Pentecost is sometimes called the birthday of the Christian Church!
pentecost.try: Hum a happy church hymn. Say "{name}!" and share a smile.

mahavirJayanti.about: Mahavir Jayanti celebrates Lord Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism. Jains visit temples and remember ahimsa (non-violence), truth, and kindness.
mahavirJayanti.funFact: Did you know? Jains try not to harm even tiny insects — that is deep respect for life!
mahavirJayanti.try: Walk gently so you do not step on ants. Say "{name}!" and smile peacefully.

paryushan.about: Paryushan is an important Jain festival of reflection, fasting, forgiveness, and self-improvement lasting several days.
paryushan.funFact: Did you know? During Paryushan people ask "Micchami Dukkadam" — please forgive my mistakes!
paryushan.try: Say sorry kindly for a small mistake. Say "{name}!" and forgive someone too.

jainDiwali.about: Jain Diwali remembers Lord Mahavira attaining nirvana (moksha). Jains light lamps, pray, and celebrate spiritual victory with calm devotion.
jainDiwali.funFact: Did you know? For Jains, Diwali lights also honor knowledge and liberation!
jainDiwali.try: Light an imaginary diya slowly. Say "{name}!" and sit quietly for five breaths.

kshamavani.about: Kshamavani is the Jain day of forgiveness at the end of Paryushan. People politely seek and grant forgiveness to clear hearts and start fresh.
kshamavani.funFact: Did you know? Forgiveness makes friendships stronger — that is the soft power of Kshamavani!
kshamavani.try: Say "Please forgive me" and "I forgive you." Then say "{name}!" with a smile.

buddhaPurnima.about: Buddha Purnima (Vesak) celebrates the birth, enlightenment, and passing of Lord Buddha. Buddhists visit temples, light lamps, and practice peace and kindness.
buddhaPurnima.funFact: Did you know? Bodh Gaya is where Buddha attained enlightenment under a peepal tree!
buddhaPurnima.try: Sit cross-legged quietly. Say "{name}!" and take three slow breaths.

losar.about: Losar is the Tibetan and Himalayan New Year celebrated in Ladakh, Sikkim, and Tibetan communities with dances, butter lamps, special foods, and family visits.
losar.funFact: Did you know? Losar house cleaning is important — people sweep away old luck for a fresh year!
losar.try: Sweep your room corner carefully. Say "{name}!" and welcome new happiness.

asalhaPuja.about: Asalha Puja (Dhamma Day) remembers Buddha's first sermon after enlightenment. Buddhists listen to teachings about the Four Noble Truths and kindness.
asalhaPuja.funFact: Did you know? This day also begins the monastic Rains Retreat (Vassa) in many Buddhist places!
asalhaPuja.try: Listen quietly for ten seconds. Say "{name}!" and share one wise kind thought.

sagaDawa.about: Saga Dawa is a sacred Buddhist month in Himalayan regions marking Buddha's birth, enlightenment, and parinirvana. People pray, give charity, and avoid harming animals.
sagaDawa.funFact: Did you know? Pilgrims often walk around sacred sites spinning prayer wheels during Saga Dawa!
sagaDawa.try: Spin your hand like a prayer wheel. Say "{name}!" and wish peace for everyone.

navroz.about: Navroz (Nowruz) is the Parsi New Year and spring festival. Families clean homes, wear new clothes, visit the fire temple, and enjoy festive meals.
navroz.funFact: Did you know? Navroz is also celebrated by many cultures along the Silk Road as the start of spring!
navroz.try: Smell an imaginary flower. Say "{name}!" and wish spring joy to someone.

pateti.about: Pateti is a Parsi day of repentance before New Year. People reflect on mistakes, ask forgiveness, and prepare to start afresh with good deeds.
pateti.funFact: Did you know? Saying sorry and fixing mistakes is the heart of Pateti!
pateti.try: Fix one small mistake kindly. Say "{name}!" and start fresh.

khordadSal.about: Khordad Sal celebrates the birthday of Prophet Zarathustra (Zoroaster). Parsi communities gather for special prayers and cultural joy.
khordadSal.funFact: Did you know? Zoroastrianism is one of the world's oldest religions, with India's Parsi community keeping it alive!
khordadSal.try: Light an imaginary lamp of truth. Say "{name}!" and smile brightly.

hornbillFestival.about: Hornbill Festival in Nagaland showcases tribes' dances, crafts, music, and food. It is called the Festival of Festivals and teaches pride in Naga culture.
hornbillFestival.funFact: Did you know? It is named after the hornbill bird, respected in Naga folklore!
hornbillFestival.try: Dance one strong tribal step. Say "{name}!" and flap your arms like a proud bird.

wangalaFestival.about: Wangala is the Garo tribe's harvest festival in Meghalaya, thanking the sun god with drums, dancing, and thanksgiving ceremonies.
wangalaFestival.funFact: Did you know? Wangala is also called the 100 Drums Festival because of its powerful drum beats!
wangalaFestival.try: Drum on your knees — boom boom! Say "{name}!" and thank the sun.

chapcharKut.about: Chapchar Kut is Mizoram's spring festival after clearing forests for farming. People wear traditional clothes, dance the Cheraw (bamboo dance), and celebrate community joy.
chapcharKut.funFact: Did you know? In Cheraw dance, dancers step between moving bamboo poles without getting caught!
chapcharKut.try: Hop carefully between imaginary bamboo poles. Say "{name}!" and giggle.

losoong.about: Losoong (Namsoong) is the Sikkimese harvest and New Year festival with masked dances, archery contests, and feasts celebrating the year's crops.
losoong.funFact: Did you know? Chaam dances with colorful masks are a highlight of Losoong!
losoong.try: Pretend to pull a bow for archery. Say "{name}!" and cheer for a bullseye.

positionsDirections.title: Positions & Directions
positionsDirections.description: Tap a card and watch the little chick act out up, down, inside, behind and many more!
positionsDirections.listHint: Tap a lesson to watch it come alive

basicPositions.title: Basic Positions
basicPositions.subtitle: Learn where things are: up, down, in, out, and more

relativePositions.title: Relative Positions
relativePositions.subtitle: See how one thing sits or moves beside another

movementDirections.title: Movement Directions
movementDirections.subtitle: Go, turn, climb, jump, walk, and run

distancePlace.title: Distance & Place
distancePlace.subtitle: Talk about places that are close, distant, here, or there

orderHeight.title: Order & Height
orderHeight.subtitle: Compare what comes first, last, higher, or lower

compass.title: Compass Directions
compass.subtitle: Meet north, south, east, and west

up.name: Up
up.caption: The little chick hops up, up, up!
up.about: Up means toward a higher place, like the sky or ceiling. When a balloon rises or you lift your hands, it moves up.
up.funFact: Did you know? Rockets zoom up so fast that they can leave the Earth and fly all the way into space!
up.try: Stretch your arms up high like a tall tree, jump up three times, and shout "Up, up, up!"

down.name: Down
down.caption: The little chick floats down to the ground!
down.about: Down means toward a lower place or the ground. Rain falls down from clouds, and a ball can roll down a hill.
down.funFact: Did you know? A raindrop can fall down from a cloud that is higher than a whole mountain!
down.try: Touch your toes and say "down". Then watch a leaf or a feather float slowly down to the floor.

left.name: Left
left.caption: The chick walks to the left side!
left.about: Left is one side of your body, where your left hand and foot are. Moving to that side means going left.
left.funFact: Did you know? Hold up both hands — your left thumb and first finger make the letter "L" for Left!
left.try: Wave your left hand, stamp your left foot, and take two small steps to the left. You did it!

right.name: Right
right.caption: The chick runs to the right side!
right.about: Right is the side of your body opposite your left side. Moving toward your right hand means going right.
right.funFact: Did you know? When people shake hands to say hello, most people all over the world use their right hand!
right.try: Wave your right hand, hop on your right foot, and place a toy on your right side.

inside.name: Inside
inside.caption: The chick is sitting inside the basket!
inside.about: Inside means within something or surrounded by it. A toy in a box and juice in a glass are both inside.
inside.funFact: Did you know? A kangaroo mom carries her baby inside a cozy pocket on her tummy called a pouch!
inside.try: Put your favorite toy inside a box, close the lid, then open it and say "My toy is inside!"

outside.name: Outside
outside.caption: The chick hopped outside the basket!
outside.about: Outside means not inside a place or container. When you leave the house for the garden, you are outside.
outside.funFact: Did you know? Butterflies and birds live outside all the time — the big sky is their roof!
outside.try: Put a toy inside a basket, then take it out, place it next to the basket and say "Now it is outside!"

under.name: Under
under.caption: The chick is safe under the umbrella!
under.about: Under means below something, often with it directly overhead. A cat can hide under a bed, and you stand under an umbrella.
under.funFact: Did you know? Under the ground, tiny ants build big cities with many little rooms and tunnels!
under.try: Crawl under a table like a little cat, then hide a toy under a blanket and find it again.

behind.name: Behind
behind.caption: Peek-a-boo! The chick is hiding behind the tree!
behind.about: Behind means at the back of a person or thing. If you hide behind a tree, the tree is in front of you.
behind.funFact: Did you know? Baby ducklings love to walk behind their mother in one neat, wobbly line!
behind.try: Play peek-a-boo! Hide behind a door or a sofa, then pop out and say "I was behind it!"

near.name: Near
near.caption: The chick is standing near the house!
near.about: Near means only a short distance away. Your pillow is near your head, and a cup may sit near your plate.
near.funFact: Did you know? The Moon is the nearest neighbor of our Earth in space — that is why it looks so big and bright!
near.try: Put two toys near each other, then stand near a window and look at the sky.

far.name: Far
far.caption: The chick flew far away from the house!
far.about: Far means a long distance away. Mountains and stars may look small because they are far from you.
far.funFact: Did you know? The Sun looks small, but it is very, very far away — sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach us!
far.try: Roll a ball far across the room, then wave to something far away, like a tree or a cloud.

between.name: Between
between.caption: The chick is standing between the two trees!
between.about: Between means in the space separating two things. Your nose is between your eyes, and a bridge can stretch between two riverbanks.
between.funFact: Did you know? A sandwich tastes yummy because the filling sits between two slices of bread!
between.try: Sit between two family members, or place a toy between two pillows and say "It is between!"

beside.name: Beside
beside.caption: The two puppies are sitting beside each other!
beside.about: Beside means next to something, usually at its side. Two friends sitting side by side are beside each other.
beside.funFact: Did you know? Penguins stand beside each other in big huddles to stay cozy and warm!
beside.try: Sit beside your favorite toy, then place your shoes beside each other in a neat pair.

middle.name: Middle
middle.caption: The chick is in the middle — the rabbit and the turtle are on its sides!
middle.about: The middle is the part between the beginning and the end or between two sides. The filling in a sandwich sits in the middle.
middle.funFact: Did you know? Your belly button is right in the middle of your tummy!
middle.try: Line up three toys and point to the one in the middle. Then stand in the middle of the room!

around.name: Around
around.caption: The butterfly is flying around the flower!
around.about: Around means on many sides of something or moving in a path that circles it. Walking around a tree can bring you back to where you started.
around.funFact: Did you know? The Earth goes around the Sun, and one full round trip takes a whole year!
around.try: Walk around a chair three times, then spin around gently one time. Whee!

top.name: Top
top.caption: The chick has reached the top!
top.about: The top is the highest part of something. A hill, a ladder, and your head all have a top.
top.funFact: A mountain's top is often called its summit or peak.
top.try: Point to the top of a door, then the top of your head.

bottom.name: Bottom
bottom.caption: The chick waits at the bottom of the ladder.
bottom.about: The bottom is the lowest part of something, opposite its top. The bottom of a cup rests on the table.
bottom.funFact: The bottom of a cup supports everything poured into it.
bottom.try: Touch the bottom of a box and say "bottom."

center.name: Center
center.caption: The chick stands in the center of the circle.
center.about: The center is the point in the middle, equally far from opposite edges. A dot in the middle of a circle marks its center.
center.funFact: The center of a round target is called the bullseye.
center.try: Draw a circle and place one dot in its center.

front.name: Front
front.caption: The engine is at the front of the train.
front.about: The front is the side that faces or leads the way. Your face is on the front of your body, and an engine may lead a train.
front.funFact: A train driver usually sits in the front engine.
front.try: Point to the front of a book and then your front.

back.name: Back
back.caption: The backpack rests on the chick's back.
back.about: The back is the side opposite the front. Your backpack rests behind your chest, on your back.
back.funFact: A backpack is named for the place where you carry it.
back.try: Put both hands behind you and touch your back.

above.name: Above
above.caption: The bird is above the tree.
above.about: Above means at a higher level than something else. A bird flying higher than a tree is above it, even without touching it.
above.funFact: Clouds are above the ground because they float in the atmosphere.
above.try: Hold one hand above the other without touching.

below.name: Below
below.caption: The ant is below the flower.
below.about: Below means at a lower level than something else. Roots are below the soil, while flowers grow higher up.
below.funFact: Tree roots grow below the soil while branches grow above it.
below.try: Place a pencil below a book.

over.name: Over
over.caption: The butterfly flies over the house.
over.about: Over means above something and can describe crossing it. A bird can fly over a roof from one side to the other.
over.funFact: Bridges let people travel over rivers safely.
over.try: Move your hand over a pillow from side to side.

in.name: In
in.caption: The ball rolls in through the opening.
in.about: In means entering a place or being within it. A ball goes in when it rolls through a box opening.
in.funFact: A letter goes in an envelope before it is mailed.
in.try: Drop a soft ball in a basket.

out.name: Out
out.caption: The ball rolls out of the box.
out.about: Out means leaving the inside of a place or container. A toy comes out when you remove it from a bag.
out.funFact: A chick comes out of its shell when it hatches.
out.try: Take a toy out of a bag.

on.name: On
on.caption: The bright light is on!
on.about: On can mean that something is working or touching a surface. A lamp is on when it shines, and a book can rest on a table.
on.funFact: A closed electric circuit lets a lamp switch on.
on.try: With permission, switch a room light on.

off.name: Off
off.caption: The lamp is off and the room is calm.
off.about: Off can mean that something has stopped working or is no longer on a surface. A lamp is off when it is not shining.
off.funFact: Switching lights off when unused saves electricity.
off.try: With permission, switch a light off.

nextTo.name: Next To
nextTo.caption: The chick sits next to the chair.
nextTo.about: Next to means immediately beside something, with little space between. Two blocks touching side by side are next to each other.
nextTo.funFact: Words next to each other are neighbors on a page.
nextTo.try: Place two blocks next to each other.

among.name: Among
among.caption: The sunflower grows among many flowers.
among.about: Among means surrounded by three or more people or things. One red flower in a patch of yellow flowers grows among them.
among.funFact: A bee may search among many blossoms for nectar.
among.try: Hide a red block among several blue blocks.

inFrontOf.name: In Front Of
inFrontOf.caption: The chick stands in front of the house.
inFrontOf.about: In front of means on the forward-facing side of something. If you stand before a chair and face it, you are in front of the chair.
inFrontOf.funFact: A crossing guard stands in front of traffic to help people cross safely.
inFrontOf.try: Stand in front of a chair and wave.

across.name: Across
across.caption: The chick walks across from one side to the other.
across.about: Across means going from one side of a space to the other. You walk across a rug when you start at one edge and reach the opposite edge.
across.funFact: A bridge can carry a road across a river.

opposite.name: Opposite
opposite.caption: The rabbit and chick face opposite sides.
opposite.about: Opposite can mean directly across from something or facing a completely different direction. Up and down are opposite directions.
opposite.funFact: North and south are opposite compass directions.
opposite.try: Point up, then point in the opposite direction.

atTheCorner.name: At the Corner
atTheCorner.caption: The chick waits at the corner of the house.
atTheCorner.about: A corner is the point where two edges or sides meet. A square has a corner at each of its four pointed turns.
atTheCorner.try: Point to every corner of a sheet of paper.

atTheEdge.name: At the Edge
atTheEdge.caption: The chick stops safely at the edge.
atTheEdge.about: The edge is the boundary where a surface ends. The edge of a table runs all the way around its top.
atTheEdge.funFact: A coin has a face on each side and an edge around it.
atTheEdge.try: Trace the edge of a book with one finger.

goUp.name: Go Up
goUp.caption: The chick goes up toward the sky.
goUp.about: Go up means move from a lower place to a higher one. Climbing a step or rising in a lift takes you up.
goUp.funFact: Hot-air balloons go up when the air inside is heated.
goUp.try: Walk up one safe step with a grown-up.

goDown.name: Go Down
goDown.caption: The chick goes down toward the ground.
goDown.about: Go down means move from a higher place to a lower one. Sliding from the top of a slide takes you down.
goDown.funFact: Water goes down a slide because gravity pulls it.
goDown.try: Move your hand slowly down from your head to your knee.

goLeft.name: Go Left
goLeft.caption: The chick follows the path to the left.
goLeft.about: Go left means travel toward your left-hand side. A left-pointing arrow shows which way to go.
goLeft.funFact: Direction signs use arrows so people know which way to go.
goLeft.try: Take two small steps to your left.

goRight.name: Go Right
goRight.caption: The chick follows the path to the right.
goRight.about: Go right means travel toward your right-hand side. A right-pointing arrow guides you in that direction.
goRight.funFact: Road arrows help drivers choose the correct direction.
goRight.try: Take two small steps to your right.

goStraight.name: Go Straight
goStraight.caption: The chick walks straight ahead.
goStraight.about: Go straight means continue forward without turning left or right. Following a straight path keeps you moving in the same direction.
goStraight.funFact: A ruler helps us draw a straight line.
goStraight.try: Follow a straight line of floor tiles.

turnLeft.name: Turn Left
turnLeft.caption: The little car turns left.
turnLeft.about: Turn left means change direction toward your left side. Your body faces a new way after the turn.
turnLeft.funFact: Drivers use turn signals before turning so others can prepare.
turnLeft.try: Face forward, then slowly turn left.

turnRight.name: Turn Right
turnRight.caption: The little car turns right.
turnRight.about: Turn right means change direction toward your right side. A curved right arrow can show where to turn.
turnRight.funFact: A right-turn arrow bends toward the right.
turnRight.try: Face forward, then slowly turn right.

turnAround.name: Turn Around
turnAround.caption: The chick turns to face the other way.
turnAround.about: Turn around means rotate until you face the other way. A half turn makes what was behind you appear in front.
turnAround.funFact: A half turn changes the direction you face.

moveForward.name: Move Forward
moveForward.caption: The bicycle moves forward.
moveForward.about: Move forward means travel in the direction you are facing. Walking toward what is in front of you moves you forward.
moveForward.funFact: Pedaling turns a bicycle's rear wheel and moves it forward.
moveForward.try: Move a toy car forward along a line.

moveBackward.name: Move Backward
moveBackward.caption: The bicycle rolls backward carefully.
moveBackward.about: Move backward means travel toward the space behind you without turning around. You should always check that the path behind you is clear.
moveBackward.funFact: Some vehicles beep while reversing to warn nearby people.
moveBackward.try: Slide a toy backward without turning it.

climbUp.name: Climb Up
climbUp.caption: The climber climbs up the ladder.
climbUp.about: Climb up means use your hands or feet to reach a higher place. Moving rung by rung on a ladder takes you upward.
climbUp.funFact: Geckos can climb walls using millions of tiny hairs on their toes.
climbUp.try: Pretend to climb an invisible ladder.

climbDown.name: Climb Down
climbDown.caption: The climber comes down one step at a time.
climbDown.about: Climb down means carefully move from a higher place to a lower one. Taking one rung or step at a time helps you descend safely.
climbDown.funFact: Climbers keep three points of contact for steadier movement.
climbDown.try: Move your hands down an imaginary ladder.

jumpUp.name: Jump Up
jumpUp.caption: The frog springs up from the ground.
jumpUp.about: Jump up means push against the ground and rise into the air. Your feet leave the ground for a moment before you land.
jumpUp.funFact: Frogs have strong back legs that help them jump.
jumpUp.try: Bend your knees and make one gentle jump up.

jumpDown.name: Jump Down
jumpDown.caption: The frog jumps down to a lower spot.
jumpDown.about: Jump down means leap from a higher safe spot to a lower one. Bending your knees can help you land gently.
jumpDown.funFact: Cats bend their legs when landing to absorb impact.
jumpDown.try: Make your fingers jump down from one book to the floor.

stepForward.name: Step Forward
stepForward.caption: One foot takes a step forward.
stepForward.about: Step forward means place one foot ahead of where it was. Your body moves a little closer to what is in front of you.
stepForward.funFact: Walking alternates one foot and then the other.

stepBack.name: Step Back
stepBack.caption: One foot takes a step back.
stepBack.about: Step back means move one step toward the space behind you. Check behind yourself first so your step is safe.
stepBack.funFact: Stepping back can give you more room to see a large picture.
stepBack.try: Check behind you, then take one careful step back.

walkAround.name: Walk Around
walkAround.caption: The chick walks around the tree.
walkAround.about: Walk around means follow a path that circles an object. You can walk around a chair without crossing through it.
walkAround.funFact: A path around a park may finish where it began.
walkAround.try: Walk once around a chair without touching it.

runTowards.name: Run Towards
runTowards.caption: The runner moves towards the finish flag.
runTowards.about: Run towards means move quickly in the direction of a person, place, or goal. The distance to that goal becomes smaller as you run.
runTowards.funFact: Runners look towards the finish line to stay on course.
runTowards.try: Point towards a safe goal and march to it.

moveAway.name: Move Away
moveAway.caption: The chick moves away from the house.
moveAway.about: Move away means make the space between you and something else larger. As you move away from a house, it appears farther behind you.
moveAway.funFact: An object's sound usually becomes quieter as you move away from it.
moveAway.try: Move a toy away from a book and watch the gap grow.

close.name: Close
close.caption: The teddy and chick are close together.
close.about: Close means only a small distance apart. Two toys with a tiny gap between them are close together.
close.funFact: Close objects often look larger than the same objects far away.
close.try: Bring your hands close without touching.

distant.name: Distant
distant.caption: The mountain looks distant from the house.
distant.about: Distant means a long way away. A distant mountain may look small even though it is very large.
distant.funFact: Distant mountains can look blue because of air and scattered light.
distant.try: Look through a window and spot something distant.

here.name: Here
here.caption: The chick says, "I am here!"
here.about: Here means the place where the speaker is now. When you point beside your feet, you are showing where here is.
here.funFact: Pointing helps show exactly where "here" is.
here.try: Point beside your feet and say "here."

there.name: There
there.caption: The chick points to a place over there.
there.about: There means a place away from the speaker. You can point across the room to show a place over there.
there.funFact: The meaning of "there" changes when the speaker moves.
there.try: Point across the room and say "there."

everywhere.name: Everywhere
everywhere.caption: Sparkles appear everywhere around Earth.
everywhere.about: Everywhere means in all places or throughout every part of a place. If toys cover the whole room, they seem to be everywhere.
everywhere.funFact: Air is everywhere around us, even though we cannot see it.
everywhere.try: Look around and name a color you can see everywhere.

somewhere.name: Somewhere
somewhere.caption: The missing star is somewhere on the map.
somewhere.about: Somewhere means in a place that is unknown or not named. A hidden toy is somewhere in the room until you find its exact spot.
somewhere.funFact: A treasure hunt begins when something is hidden somewhere.
somewhere.try: Hide a block somewhere nearby for a friend to find.

nowhere.name: Nowhere
nowhere.caption: The chick searches, but the toy is nowhere here.
nowhere.about: Nowhere means not in any place being searched or discussed. If a toy is nowhere in the box, you will not find it there.
nowhere.funFact: If a puzzle piece is nowhere on the table, it may be stored elsewhere.
nowhere.try: Look in an empty box and say "It is nowhere inside."

higher.name: Higher
higher.caption: The left balloon floats higher than the other.
higher.about: Higher compares two levels and means farther above. A balloon near the ceiling is higher than one near the floor.
higher.funFact: Warm air can make a balloon rise higher.
higher.try: Hold one hand higher than the other.

lower.name: Lower
lower.caption: One balloon is lower than the other.
lower.about: Lower compares two levels and means farther down. A block on the floor is lower than one on a table.
lower.funFact: A low musical note has a slower vibration than a high note.
lower.try: Place one block lower than a block on a book.

highest.name: Highest
highest.caption: The gold trophy is the highest of all.
highest.about: Highest means above every other item in a group. The tallest of three towers reaches the highest point.
highest.funFact: Mount Everest has Earth's highest summit above sea level.
highest.try: Build three towers and point to the highest.

lowest.name: Lowest
lowest.caption: The ant is at the lowest level.
lowest.about: Lowest means below every other item in a group. Of several shelves, the one nearest the floor is the lowest.
lowest.funFact: The lowest floor of a building may be a basement.
lowest.try: Arrange three toys and point to the lowest.

upper.name: Upper
upper.caption: The window is in the upper part of the house.
upper.about: Upper describes the higher part of something. The upper half of a page is the part nearer its top.
upper.funFact: Your upper arm lies between your shoulder and elbow.
upper.try: Point to the upper half of a page.

first.name: First
first.caption: The gold medal marks first place.
first.about: First means before everyone or everything else in an order. The child at the front of a line is first.
first.funFact: The first month of the year is January.
first.try: Line up three toys and name the first.

last.name: Last
last.caption: The turtle is last in the line.
last.about: Last means after everyone or everything else in an order. The final toy in a row is last.
last.funFact: The last page finishes a story.
last.try: Line up three books and point to the last.

north.name: North
north.caption: The compass needle points north.
north.about: North is one of the four main compass directions. A compass or map can help you find which way is north.
north.funFact: Most maps place north at the top.
north.try: Find north with a compass and point that way.

south.name: South
south.caption: The compass shows the way south.
south.about: South is the main compass direction opposite north. On most maps, south is shown toward the bottom.
south.try: Find south on a compass rose.

east.name: East
east.caption: The compass points east towards sunrise.
east.about: East is the main compass direction opposite west. The Sun appears near the eastern horizon in the morning.
east.funFact: The Sun appears to rise in the east because Earth rotates.
east.try: Point to east on a map or compass.

west.name: West
west.caption: The compass points west towards sunset.
west.about: West is the main compass direction opposite east. The Sun appears near the western horizon in the evening.
west.funFact: The Sun appears to set in the west.
west.try: Find west on a compass rose.

goodHabits.title: Good Habits & Hygiene
goodHabits.description: Pick a colorful card. Learn why each habit helps you grow happy and strong.
goodHabits.listHint: Tap a habit to learn why it matters

encouragement.0: You are learning to care for yourself — awesome!
encouragement.1: Every small habit makes a big difference.
encouragement.4: Proud of you for learning good habits!

personalHygiene.title: Personal Hygiene
personalHygiene.subtitle: Keep your body fresh, clean, and healthy every day

brushTeeth.about: Brushing your teeth removes food bits and tiny germs. Clean teeth help you smile, chew food, and keep your mouth fresh.
brushTeeth.funFact: Did you know? The hard outer part of your teeth is very strong. Brushing helps keep it healthy.
brushTeeth.try: With a grown-up, brush your teeth for two minutes. Brush every tooth gently, then rinse and say "{name}!"

brushTeethTwice.about: Brushing twice a day keeps your teeth clean. Brush once in the morning and once before bed.
brushTeethTwice.funFact: Did you know? Germs can stay on your teeth at night. Brushing before bed helps remove them.
brushTeethTwice.try: Make a chart for morning and bedtime brushing. Tick both boxes today and say "{name}!"

washHands.about: Washing hands with soap and water removes dirt and germs you cannot see. Clean hands keep your food safe and help you stay healthy.
washHands.funFact: Did you know? Soap helps germs wash away when you rinse with water.
washHands.try: Wash your hands with soap for twenty seconds. Dry them and say "{name}!"

washHandsBeforeEating.about: Washing hands before eating keeps dirt and germs away from your food. Clean hands help your tummy stay healthy.
washHandsBeforeEating.funFact: Did you know? Your hands touch many things each day. Washing before meals keeps food clean.
washHandsBeforeEating.try: Before your next snack, wash your hands with soap. Count to twenty, then say "{name}!"

washHandsAfterToilet.about: After using the toilet, germs can stay on your hands. Washing with soap removes them so they do not spread to your face or food.
washHandsAfterToilet.funFact: Did you know? Flushing cleans the toilet. Washing your hands cleans your hands. Both steps keep you healthy.
washHandsAfterToilet.try: After using the toilet today, wash your hands with soap. Rinse well and say "{name}!"

washHandsAfterPlaying.about: Playing outside can leave dirt on your hands. After play, washing removes sand, grass, and germs from toys.
washHandsAfterPlaying.funFact: Did you know? Balls, swings, and toys can carry germs. Washing after play keeps you clean.
washHandsAfterPlaying.try: After playing today, wash your hands with soap. Then say "{name}!"

washFace.about: Washing your face removes dust and dirt from your skin. A clean face feels fresh and ready for the day.
washFace.funFact: Did you know? Your face skin is soft and needs gentle care. Clean water helps it stay healthy.
washFace.try: Wash your face gently with clean water. Pat it dry and say "{name}!"

takeBath.about: A bath washes sweat and dirt off your skin. Warm water and soap help you feel clean and comfortable.
takeBath.funFact: Did you know? Your skin is the largest part of your body. Bathing keeps it clean and healthy.
takeBath.try: Ask a grown-up to help you take a bath. Wash your body and toes, then say "{name}!"

shampooHair.about: Shampoo washes oil and dust from your hair and scalp. Clean hair feels light and smells fresh.
shampooHair.funFact: Did you know? Your scalp is skin under your hair. Shampoo keeps it clean so hair can grow well.
shampooHair.try: With a grown-up, shampoo and rinse your hair. Pat it dry and say "{name}!"

combHair.about: Combing removes tangles so hair sits neat. Start gently at the ends to avoid pulling.
combHair.funFact: Did you know? Combing spreads natural oils through your hair. This keeps hair smooth and healthy.
combHair.try: Comb your hair slowly once today. Be gentle with knots and say "{name}!"

trimNails.about: Trimming nails keeps them short and smooth. Short nails do not scratch and are easier to keep clean.
trimNails.funFact: Did you know? Nails grow a little every day. Regular trimming keeps dirt from hiding underneath.
trimNails.try: Ask a grown-up to check if your nails need a trim. Then say "{name}!"

keepNailsClean.about: Clean nails have less dirt underneath. Scrubbing nail tips while washing hands keeps your hands tidy.
keepNailsClean.funFact: Did you know? Germs can hide under long or dirty nails. Soap and a soft brush help clean them.
keepNailsClean.try: Wash your hands and gently scrub under your nails. Show a grown-up and say "{name}!"

wearCleanClothes.about: Clean clothes feel soft on your skin. Fresh clothes keep you comfortable at school, the park, or home.
wearCleanClothes.funFact: Did you know? Clothes can hold dirt and smell even when they look fine. Clean clothes feel better.
wearCleanClothes.try: Pick a clean outfit today with a grown-up. Put it on and say "{name}!"

changeClothesDaily.about: Changing clothes each day gives you fresh, clean fabric. New clothes help your skin breathe and feel good.
changeClothesDaily.funFact: Did you know? Wearing the same clothes every day can cause itching. Fresh clothes help you feel better.
changeClothesDaily.try: Put worn clothes in the laundry basket tonight. Tomorrow wear clean clothes and say "{name}!"

wearCleanSocks.about: Clean socks keep your feet comfortable. Fresh socks soak up sweat and help your shoes stay nice.
wearCleanSocks.funFact: Did you know? Feet sweat during the day. Clean socks help keep feet and shoes fresh.
wearCleanSocks.try: Choose a clean pair of socks today. Wiggle your toes and say "{name}!"

wearCleanShoes.about: Clean shoes protect your feet from dirt and sharp things. Wiping soles keeps shoes and floors cleaner.
wearCleanShoes.funFact: Did you know? Shoes carry outdoor dirt on their bottoms. Clean shoes protect your feet and home.
wearCleanShoes.try: Wipe or brush your shoes with a grown-up's help. Put them on and say "{name}!"

keepHairClean.about: Keeping hair clean means washing it regularly. Clean hair feels fresh and helps stop an itchy scalp.
keepHairClean.funFact: Did you know? Hats, pillows, and wind can leave dust in hair. Regular washing keeps hair clean.
keepHairClean.try: Look at your hair in a mirror today. Wash it if needed with help, then say "{name}!"

useSoapProperly.about: Using soap properly means rubbing it on all parts of your hands. Cover palms, backs, between fingers, and under nails, then rinse well.
useSoapProperly.funFact: Did you know? Rinsing with water alone leaves many germs behind. Soap helps remove them.
useSoapProperly.try: Wash your hands with soap on every part for twenty seconds. Then say "{name}!"
