useHandSanitizer.about: Hand sanitizer helps when soap and water are not nearby. Rub it on your hands until they feel dry.
useHandSanitizer.funFact: Did you know? Sanitizer works best on clean, dry hands. If hands are very dirty, use soap and water.
useHandSanitizer.try: With a grown-up's okay, rub sanitizer on your hands until dry. Then say "{name}!"

useHandkerchief.about: A clean handkerchief or tissue catches sneezes and sniffles. Using one keeps germs off your hands.
useHandkerchief.funFact: Did you know? People used cloth handkerchiefs before paper tissues. Both help keep noses clean.
useHandkerchief.try: Carry a clean tissue today. Use it for one sniffle and say "{name}!"

coverMouthCoughing.about: Covering your mouth when you cough stops germs from spreading. Use your elbow or a tissue to protect others.
coverMouthCoughing.funFact: Did you know? A cough sends tiny drops into the air. Covering your mouth keeps others safe.
coverMouthCoughing.try: Practice coughing into your elbow once. Then say "{name}!"

coverNoseSneezing.about: Covering your nose when you sneeze catches germs before they spread. Use a tissue or your elbow.
coverNoseSneezing.funFact: Did you know? A sneeze is very fast and sends germs into the air. Covering up protects people nearby.
coverNoseSneezing.try: Practice sneezing into your elbow once. Then say "{name}!"

throwTissueDustbin.about: Used tissues hold germs and should go in the bin. Throwing them away keeps desks and floors clean.
throwTissueDustbin.funFact: Did you know? A used tissue left on a table can spread germs. The bin is the right place for it.
throwTissueDustbin.try: Put your next used tissue straight in the bin. Then say "{name}!"

useToiletProperly.about: Using the toilet properly means sitting or standing safely and keeping the area tidy. Good habits keep the bathroom clean for everyone.
useToiletProperly.funFact: Did you know? Toilets are shared at home and school. Using them carefully shows respect for others.
useToiletProperly.try: Follow toilet steps carefully with a grown-up's help. When done, say "{name}!"

flushToilet.about: Flushing sends waste away and keeps the toilet clean. One push of the handle finishes the job.
flushToilet.funFact: Did you know? Forgetting to flush leaves the bathroom dirty for the next person. Flushing keeps it clean.
flushToilet.try: After using the toilet today, flush and wash your hands. Then say "{name}!"

keepBathroomClean.about: Keeping the bathroom clean means wiping spills and hanging towels. A tidy bathroom feels safer and fresher.
keepBathroomClean.funFact: Did you know? Wet floors can be slippery. A neat bathroom helps everyone stay safe.
keepBathroomClean.try: Hang your towel and wipe one small spill with help. Then say "{name}!"

washFeetBeforeSleep.about: Washing feet before sleep removes dust and sweat from the day. Clean feet feel cool and keep bedsheets fresh.
washFeetBeforeSleep.funFact: Did you know? Feet collect dirt all day long. A bedtime wash keeps them clean.
washFeetBeforeSleep.try: Tonight wash your feet with mild soap. Dry between your toes and say "{name}!"

drinkCleanWater.about: Clean drinking water keeps your body healthy without germs. Filtered, boiled, or bottled water chosen by grown-ups is safest.
drinkCleanWater.funFact: Did you know? Your body needs a lot of water. Clean water helps your brain and body work well.
drinkCleanWater.try: Drink a glass of clean water with a grown-up's help. Then say "{name}!"

keepBodyClean.about: Keeping your body clean means bathing, washing hands, and wearing fresh clothes. A clean body feels comfortable and healthy.
keepBodyClean.funFact: Did you know? Clean skin makes it harder for germs to stay on your body.
keepBodyClean.try: Today do one clean-body step: take a bath, wash your face, or wear clean clothes. Then say "{name}!"

doNotSpit.about: Do not spit on floors, roads, or playgrounds. Spit can spread germs. Use a sink or tissue instead.
doNotSpit.funFact: Did you know? Spit can carry germs that make people sick. Keeping it off shared spaces helps everyone.
doNotSpit.try: If you need to spit today, use a sink or tissue only. Then say "{name}!"

keepEarsClean.about: Keeping ears clean means washing the outer part gently. Do not put anything deep inside your ear.
keepEarsClean.funFact: Did you know? Ears make a little wax that protects them. Only grown-ups should clean deeper parts.
keepEarsClean.try: With a grown-up, gently wash the outer ear while bathing. Then say "{name}!"

keepNoseClean.about: A clean nose helps you breathe easily. Use a soft tissue and blow gently, one side at a time.
keepNoseClean.funFact: Did you know? Nose hairs and mucus catch dust before it goes deeper into your body.
keepNoseClean.try: Blow your nose gently into a tissue. Throw it in the bin, wash your hands, and say "{name}!"

useTowelAfterBath.about: Drying with a clean towel after a bath removes leftover water. A dry body feels warm and keeps clothes from getting wet.
useTowelAfterBath.funFact: Did you know? Water left on skin can cause itching. A towel helps you dry well.
useTowelAfterBath.try: After washing, pat dry with your towel. Dry your toes too, then say "{name}!"

weatherClothes.about: Weather clothes match hot, rainy, or cold days. Caps, sweaters, and raincoats help you stay comfortable outside.
weatherClothes.funFact: Did you know? Different weather needs different clothes. The right clothes keep you safe and comfortable.
weatherClothes.try: Look outside and pick clothes with a grown-up. Name the weather and say "{name}!"

goodHabits.title: Good Habits
goodHabits.subtitle: Little daily actions that make you strong and kind

wakeUpEarly.about: Waking up early gives you time to wash, eat, and get ready calmly. An early start makes the morning less rushed.
wakeUpEarly.funFact: Did you know? Morning sunlight helps your body feel awake. Opening curtains can help you wake up.
wakeUpEarly.try: Make a morning plan with a grown-up. Stretch when you wake up and say "{name}!"

sleepOnTime.about: Sleeping on time lets your body rest and grow. A regular bedtime helps you wake up feeling good.
sleepOnTime.funFact: Did you know? During sleep your brain stores what you learned that day. Enough sleep helps you remember better.
sleepOnTime.try: Choose a bedtime and put toys away five minutes early. Then say "{name}!"

makeYourBed.about: Making your bed smooths the sheets and puts the pillow in place. A neat bed makes your room look tidy.
makeYourBed.funFact: Did you know? Many people feel good when they finish one small job in the morning. Making your bed is a good start.
makeYourBed.try: Pull up the sheet and straighten the pillow. Step back and say "{name}!"

brushBeforeSleeping.about: Brushing before sleep removes food from your teeth. Night brushing protects your teeth while you sleep.
brushBeforeSleeping.funFact: Did you know? Germs like to eat leftover sugar on teeth at night. Brushing before bed helps stop them.
brushBeforeSleeping.try: Tonight brush your teeth carefully before bed. Rinse and say "{name}!"

prayEveryDay.about: Praying or sitting quietly each day can help you feel peaceful and thankful. It is a gentle habit of hope.
prayEveryDay.funFact: Did you know? Many families around the world take quiet thankful moments. Stillness can calm busy feelings.
prayEveryDay.try: Sit quietly for one minute. Think a kind wish, then say "{name}!"

exerciseDaily.about: Daily exercise moves your muscles and makes your heart work. Running, jumping, and dancing help bones grow strong.
exerciseDaily.funFact: Did you know? Moving your body helps your brain focus and feel happier after play.
exerciseDaily.try: Do ten jumps or a short dance. Then say "{name}!"

doYoga.about: Yoga uses gentle stretches, balance poses, and slow breathing. It helps your body feel flexible and your mind feel calm.
doYoga.funFact: Did you know? Some yoga poses are named after animals like cat, cow, and cobra.
doYoga.try: Try a gentle tree pose with a grown-up nearby. Breathe in and out, then say "{name}!"

readBooks.about: Reading books teaches you new words and stories. Books grow your imagination and make learning fun.
readBooks.funFact: Did you know? Reading a few pages each day builds many new words in your brain over time.
readBooks.try: Read or listen to one short story today. Point to a favorite picture and say "{name}!"

studyEveryDay.about: Studying a little every day keeps lessons fresh in your mind. Short daily practice is better than rushing before a test.
studyEveryDay.funFact: Did you know? Your brain remembers better with small daily sessions than with one long study time.
studyEveryDay.try: Study for ten minutes with a grown-up timer. When done, say "{name}!"

finishHomework.about: Finishing homework on time helps lessons stay in your mind. It also leaves more time for rest and play.
finishHomework.funFact: Did you know? Doing homework soon after school is often easier than waiting until you are very tired.
finishHomework.try: Open your bag and do one homework piece carefully. When finished, say "{name}!"

packSchoolBag.about: Packing your school bag the night before keeps books and supplies ready. This makes mornings smoother.
packSchoolBag.funFact: Did you know? Forgetting one item can slow down your morning. Packing ahead helps you be ready.
packSchoolBag.try: Tonight pack your bag with a grown-up checklist. Zip it shut and say "{name}!"

organizeSchoolBag.about: An organized bag keeps books flat and pencils easy to find. Neat packing saves time at school.
organizeSchoolBag.funFact: Did you know? Putting heavy books near your back often feels more comfortable to carry.
organizeSchoolBag.try: Empty your bag once, sort papers, and put books back neatly. Then say "{name}!"

keepThingsOrganized.about: Keeping things organized means every item has a place. This saves time and makes finding things easy.
keepThingsOrganized.funFact: Did you know? Your mind feels calmer when your room looks tidy. Clutter can feel distracting.
keepThingsOrganized.try: Put five things back in their places. Count them and say "{name}!"

putToysBack.about: Putting toys back after play keeps floors safe and toys easy to find. Tidying is part of finishing play.
putToysBack.funFact: Did you know? Lost puzzle pieces often hide under furniture. Putting toys back keeps sets complete.
putToysBack.try: Tidy up while a song plays. When the song ends, toys should be put away. Then say "{name}!"

cleanStudyTable.about: A clean study table gives you space for homework. Clear desks help you focus better.
cleanStudyTable.funFact: Did you know? A messy desk can hide erasers and papers you need. Cleaning helps you find things.
cleanStudyTable.try: Clear three things off your table now. Wipe if needed and say "{name}!"

completeWorkOnTime.about: Completing work on time means finishing tasks before the deadline. Finishing on time builds trust and leaves time for fun.
completeWorkOnTime.funFact: Did you know? Breaking a job into small steps makes it easier to finish on time.
completeWorkOnTime.try: Pick one small task and set a timer. Finish before it rings and say "{name}!"

beResponsible.about: Being responsible means doing your part at home and school. People can count on you when you do your jobs.
beResponsible.funFact: Did you know? Doing small jobs each day builds trust over time.
beResponsible.try: Choose one job you will do today, like watering a plant. Finish it and say "{name}!"

beHonest.about: Being honest means telling the truth even when it is hard. Honesty helps grown-ups help you and keeps friendships strong.
beHonest.funFact: Did you know? Telling the truth is easier than remembering many lies.
beHonest.try: Tell one small true thing kindly today. Then say "{name}!"

beKind.about: Being kind means using gentle words and helping others. Kindness makes you and others feel good.
beKind.funFact: Did you know? When you help someone, they often help someone else too.
beKind.try: Do one kind act today: give a compliment, share, or help someone. Then say "{name}!"

beHelpful.about: Being helpful means noticing when someone needs help. Carrying a bag or picking up a pencil makes life easier for others.
beHelpful.funFact: Did you know? Helping others teaches you useful skills for growing up.
beHelpful.try: Ask "How can I help?" once today. Do the small job and say "{name}!"

bePatient.about: Being patient means waiting calmly for your turn or for an answer. Patience helps you stay peaceful.
bePatient.funFact: Did you know? Plants take time to grow. Waiting calmly is an important skill too.
bePatient.try: While waiting once today, take three slow breaths. Then say "{name}!"

smileEveryDay.about: Smiling shares warmth without words. A smile can lift your mood and make others feel welcome.
smileEveryDay.funFact: Did you know? Smiling can help your brain feel calmer and happier.
smileEveryDay.try: Smile at yourself in a mirror, then at a family member. Say "{name}!"

thinkPositively.about: Thinking positively means looking for what can go well. Hopeful thoughts help you try again when things feel hard.
thinkPositively.funFact: Did you know? Your brain learns from the thoughts you repeat. Positive thoughts can make challenges feel smaller.
thinkPositively.try: Change one "I can't" into "I'll try." Say it aloud, then say "{name}!"

respectNature.about: Respecting nature means treating trees, parks, and rivers gently. Do not break branches or leave litter behind.
respectNature.funFact: Did you know? One old tree can give shade and a home for birds. Taking care of nature keeps that home safe.
respectNature.try: Pick up one piece of litter outside with a grown-up, or gently touch a leaf. Then say "{name}!"

respectAnimals.about: Respecting animals means gentle hands and quiet voices. Never hurt pets or wild animals.
respectAnimals.funFact: Did you know? Many animals understand calm body language better than loud words.
respectAnimals.try: If you meet a pet today, ask first, then pet gently. Say "{name}!"

followRules.about: Following rules keeps games fair and places safe. Rules help everyone know how to play and learn together.
followRules.funFact: Did you know? Even sports champions follow rules. Rules make games fair for everyone.
followRules.try: Name one home or class rule and follow it carefully today. Then say "{name}!"

followDailyRoutine.about: A daily routine is a plan for your day: wake, wash, eat, learn, play, and sleep. Routines help you know what comes next.
followDailyRoutine.funFact: Did you know? Routines can reduce worry because you know what to expect each day.
followDailyRoutine.try: Follow your morning steps in order once. Check them off and say "{name}!"

bePunctual.about: Being punctual means arriving when you promised. Being on time shows respect for teachers and friends.
bePunctual.funFact: Did you know? Starting on time often means finishing with less worry.
bePunctual.try: Be ready five minutes early for one plan today. Point to the clock and say "{name}!"

stayActive.about: Staying active means moving your body often. Walking, stretching, and playing help build a strong heart.
stayActive.funFact: Did you know? Sitting still too long can make your body feel stiff. Short movement breaks help.
stayActive.try: Take a ten-minute active break: march, hop, or walk. Then say "{name}!"

avoidLaziness.about: Avoiding laziness means starting small jobs instead of waiting. Even tiny steps turn hard feelings into progress.
avoidLaziness.funFact: Did you know? Energy often comes after you begin a task. The first step is the hardest.
avoidLaziness.try: Do one delayed chore for two minutes only. Then say "{name}!"

listenCarefully.about: Listening carefully means using your eyes and ears while others speak. Good listening helps you learn and makes speakers feel valued.
listenCarefully.funFact: Did you know? Your brain remembers more when you look and listen together.
listenCarefully.try: Listen to one short instruction without interrupting. Repeat it and say "{name}!"

askQuestionsPolitely.about: Asking questions politely means using words like please and waiting for a pause. Curious questions help you learn.
askQuestionsPolitely.funFact: Did you know? Scientists learn by asking questions. Polite curiosity helps discoveries happen.
askQuestionsPolitely.try: Ask one polite question today: "Please, may I know…?" Then say "{name}!"

learnNewThings.about: Learning new things stretches your brain like exercise stretches muscles. New skills make each day more interesting.
learnNewThings.funFact: Did you know? Every time you learn, your brain builds new connections.
learnNewThings.try: Learn one new word or small skill today. Show someone and say "{name}!"

practiceEveryDay.about: Practicing every day turns slow tries into smooth skills. Music, letters, sports, and drawing all improve with daily practice.
practiceEveryDay.funFact: Did you know? Champions practice small parts every day, not just once in a while.
practiceEveryDay.try: Practice one skill for five minutes. Notice one improvement and say "{name}!"

beThankful.about: Being thankful means noticing good things like food, family, and friends. Saying thank you grows joy in your heart.
beThankful.funFact: Did you know? Naming things you are thankful for can help you feel calmer and happier.
beThankful.try: Name three things you are thankful for before bed. Then say "{name}!"

healthyEating.title: Healthy Eating
healthyEating.subtitle: Fuel your body with yummy, smart food choices

eatHealthyFood.about: Healthy food gives your body what it needs to grow strong. Colorful fruits and vegetables help you play longer.
eatHealthyFood.funFact: Did you know? Different colors in food often mean different vitamins. A colorful plate is good for you.
eatHealthyFood.try: Add one healthy food to your next meal. Point to it and say "{name}!"

eatFreshFruits.about: Fresh fruits are sweet snacks full of water and vitamins. Apples, bananas, and oranges help your body stay healthy.
eatFreshFruits.funFact: Did you know? Many fruits come from farms. Eating them helps you and supports farmers.
eatFreshFruits.try: Eat one fresh fruit today. Describe how it tastes and say "{name}!"

eatGreenVegetables.about: Green vegetables like spinach, beans, and peas give your body iron and fiber. They help you feel strong, even if they taste a little different.
eatGreenVegetables.funFact: Did you know? Green vegetables get their color from chlorophyll. Plants use it to grow in sunlight.
eatGreenVegetables.try: Eat three small bites of a green vegetable today. Then say "{name}!"

drinkMilk.about: Milk gives calcium that helps bones and teeth grow strong. A glass with meals is good growing food.
drinkMilk.funFact: Did you know? Calcium in milk helps build stronger bones as you grow taller.
drinkMilk.try: Drink a glass of milk with a meal today if you may. Then say "{name}!"

drinkPlentyWater.about: Drinking plenty of water keeps your body from feeling tired or thirsty. Regular sips help you stay active.
drinkPlentyWater.funFact: Did you know? Sometimes you feel hungry when you are really thirsty. Drinking water can help.
drinkPlentyWater.try: Fill a bottle and finish it by evening with grown-up help. Then say "{name}!"

eatBreakfastDaily.about: Breakfast gives your body food after sleep. Eating breakfast helps you focus at school and feel less hungry.
eatBreakfastDaily.funFact: Did you know? Your brain works better with morning food. Skipping breakfast can make focusing harder.
eatBreakfastDaily.try: Eat breakfast tomorrow without rushing. Name two foods on your plate and say "{name}!"

eatOnTime.about: Eating on time keeps your energy steady. Regular meals help your body digest food well.
eatOnTime.funFact: Did you know? Your stomach likes eating at regular times each day.
eatOnTime.try: Sit for one meal at the usual time today. Chew calmly and say "{name}!"

washFruits.about: Washing fruits removes dust and dirt before you eat. Clean fruit is safer and tastes fresher.
washFruits.funFact: Did you know? Even fruit peels can have dirt on them. Washing first is a good habit.
washFruits.try: Wash one fruit under clean water with a grown-up. Eat it and say "{name}!"

washVegetables.about: Washing vegetables removes soil before cooking or eating. Clean vegetables keep meals safe.
washVegetables.funFact: Did you know? Leafy greens can hide dirt in their folds. A gentle wash removes it.
washVegetables.try: Help rinse one vegetable today. Then say "{name}!"

washHandsBeforeMeals.about: Washing hands before meals is the last clean step before eating. It keeps dirt and germs off your food.
washHandsBeforeMeals.funFact: Did you know? Many families wash hands together before eating. It is a healthy habit.
washHandsBeforeMeals.try: Wash with soap before your next meal. Sit down clean and say "{name}!"

chewFoodProperly.about: Chewing food properly breaks bites into small pieces. This makes swallowing easy and helps digestion start in your mouth.
chewFoodProperly.funFact: Did you know? Digestion begins when you chew. Your teeth help break food into smaller pieces.
chewFoodProperly.try: Chew one bite twenty times before swallowing. Notice how it feels and say "{name}!"

eatSlowly.about: Eating slowly helps you taste your food and notice when you feel full. Slow meals prevent tummy aches from rushing.
eatSlowly.funFact: Did you know? Your body takes a few minutes to feel full. Eating slowly helps you notice when you have had enough.
eatSlowly.try: Put the spoon down between two bites today. Eat slowly and say "{name}!"

finishYourFood.about: Finishing the food you took shows respect for the meal. Take only what you can eat so nothing is wasted.
finishYourFood.funFact: Did you know? Listening to your hunger helps you eat the right amount. Do not force yourself to eat too much.
finishYourFood.try: Take a small serving you can finish. When done, say "{name}!"

dontWasteFood.about: Not wasting food means taking what you need and saving leftovers with help. Food takes hard work to grow and cook.
dontWasteFood.funFact: Did you know? Wasted food around the world could feed many hungry people. Small careful choices at home matter.
dontWasteFood.try: Ask for a smaller serving if unsure. Finish or save leftovers with help, then say "{name}!"

eatHomemadeFood.about: Homemade food is often cooked with care and fresh ingredients. Home meals can be healthier than packaged snacks every day.
eatHomemadeFood.funFact: Did you know? Helping wash vegetables or stir food at home teaches you about cooking.
eatHomemadeFood.try: Thank the cook for one homemade dish today. Taste it carefully and say "{name}!"

avoidJunkFood.about: Avoiding too much junk food means eating chips and fried snacks less often. Occasional treats are fine, but healthy food should be most meals.
avoidJunkFood.funFact: Did you know? Some junk foods are made to taste very exciting. Your body still needs fruits and vegetables most days.
avoidJunkFood.try: Swap one junk snack for fruit or nuts today. Then say "{name}!"

avoidTooManyChocolates.about: Too many chocolates can harm your teeth and give quick energy that fades fast. Enjoy chocolate sometimes, then brush your teeth.
avoidTooManyChocolates.funFact: Did you know? Chocolate starts as cocoa beans from trees. Eating it sometimes makes it special.
avoidTooManyChocolates.try: If you have chocolate, eat a small piece. Rinse or brush later and say "{name}!"

avoidSoftDrinks.about: Soft drinks have a lot of sugar in one glass. Choosing water or milk most often keeps teeth and energy healthier.
avoidSoftDrinks.funFact: Did you know? Some soft drinks have many spoonfuls of sugar. That can stick to your teeth.
avoidSoftDrinks.try: Pick water instead of a soft drink once today. Then say "{name}!"

eatDryFruits.about: Dry fruits like almonds, raisins, and dates are small energy snacks. Chew them well and only eat age-safe amounts.
eatDryFruits.funFact: Did you know? Drying fruit makes it smaller but keeps many nutrients. A few pieces give good energy.
eatDryFruits.try: With a grown-up, eat a small handful of safe dry fruit. Chew well and say "{name}!"

eatProteinRich.about: Protein-rich foods like dal, eggs, milk, and beans help build muscles. Protein helps your body repair and grow.
eatProteinRich.funFact: Did you know? After hard play, protein foods help muscles recover and grow stronger.
eatProteinRich.try: Find one protein food on your plate today. Point to it and say "{name}!"

eatBalancedMeals.about: Balanced meals mix grains, vegetables or fruits, and proteins. This gives your body many types of nutrients.
eatBalancedMeals.funFact: Did you know? A balanced plate looks colorful. Meals with only one color may miss important vitamins.
eatBalancedMeals.try: At one meal, include three colors of food. Count them and say "{name}!"

drinkFreshJuice.about: Fresh juice from washed fruits can be a healthy treat. It is best without extra sugar added.
drinkFreshJuice.funFact: Did you know? Whole fruit has fiber that juice sometimes leaves out. Both can be part of a healthy day.
drinkFreshJuice.try: Share a small glass of fresh juice with a grown-up. Sip slowly and say "{name}!"

avoidTooMuchSugar.about: Too much sugar can harm teeth and make energy go up and then down quickly. Saving sweets for sometimes keeps meals healthy.
avoidTooMuchSugar.funFact: Did you know? Sugar can hide in sauces and cereals too. Reading labels with a grown-up helps you spot it.
avoidTooMuchSugar.try: Skip one extra sweet today. Choose fruit instead and say "{name}!"

avoidEatingWhileTv.about: Eating without TV helps you notice flavors and when you feel full. Screens can make you eat without thinking.
avoidEatingWhileTv.funFact: Did you know? People often eat more with screens on because they forget to check if they are full.
avoidEatingWhileTv.try: Eat one snack or meal with screens off. Taste carefully and say "{name}!"

useSpoonProperly.about: Using a spoon properly means lifting food gently without swinging the spoon. Good spoon use keeps tables and clothes cleaner.
useSpoonProperly.funFact: Did you know? Spoons are one of the oldest eating tools. Gentle scoops are good table manners.
useSpoonProperly.try: Practice lifting food slowly with a spoon three times. Then say "{name}!"

sitProperlyEating.about: Sitting properly while eating means feet steady, back straight, and plate close. Good posture makes swallowing safe and meals calmer.
sitProperlyEating.funFact: Did you know? Eating while standing or walking can increase choking risk. Sitting at a table is safer.
sitProperlyEating.try: Sit tall for one whole meal. Notice how chewing feels, then say "{name}!"

shareFood.about: Sharing food means offering a little food or splitting a snack when it is okay. Sharing builds friendship and shows kindness.
shareFood.funFact: Did you know? Sharing a snack can make two people happy at once.
shareFood.try: Offer to share a safe snack with someone today. Then say "{name}!"

thankYouAtTable.about: Saying thank you before leaving the table honors the cook and the meal. Grateful words show you care.
thankYouAtTable.funFact: Did you know? Many cultures teach saying thanks at the table. It is a warm habit around the world.
thankYouAtTable.try: After your next meal, say "Thank you" for the food. Then say "{name}!"

cleanliness.title: Cleanliness Habits
cleanliness.subtitle: A tidy place feels happy — start with small clean-ups

throwGarbageDustbin.about: Throwing garbage in the dustbin keeps floors and streets clean. Bins are the right place for wrappers and scraps.
throwGarbageDustbin.funFact: Did you know? Litter can blow into drains and rivers. Using bins keeps places clean.
throwGarbageDustbin.try: Throw one wrapper in the bin today. Then say "{name}!"

separateWetDry.about: Separating wet and dry waste helps recycling and composting. Peels go in wet waste; paper often goes in dry waste. Ask a grown-up which bin to use.
separateWetDry.funFact: Did you know? Mixed trash is harder to reuse. Sorting waste makes recycling easier.
separateWetDry.try: Sort one snack wrapper into the right wet or dry bin. Then say "{name}!"

keepRoomClean.about: A clean room has clear floors, a made bed, and toys in their places. Clean rooms feel peaceful and safe.
keepRoomClean.funFact: Did you know? Cleaning a little each day is easier than cleaning a big mess once a week.
keepRoomClean.try: Spend five minutes tidying your room. Look around and say "{name}!"

cleanToys.about: Cleaning toys removes sticky marks and dust. Clean toys feel nicer and last longer.
cleanToys.funFact: Did you know? Shared toys can pass germs. Wiping them after sick days helps everyone stay healthy.
cleanToys.try: Wipe two toys with a damp cloth and grown-up help. Then say "{name}!"

cleanStudyTableHabit.about: Keeping the study table clean removes dust and crumbs. A clean desk gives books and homework more space.
cleanStudyTableHabit.funFact: Did you know? Pencil dust and eraser crumbs build up over time. A weekly wipe keeps the desk ready.
cleanStudyTableHabit.try: Wipe your study table once today. Stack papers neatly and say "{name}!"

organizeBooks.about: Organizing books means standing or stacking them neatly. Ordered books are easier to find when you need them.
organizeBooks.funFact: Did you know? Libraries use systems so any book can be found. Your shelf can work the same way.
organizeBooks.try: Line up five books neatly. Look at them and say "{name}!"

organizeClothes.about: Organizing clothes keeps shirts and pants easy to find. Folded or hung clothes wrinkle less and save time in the morning.
organizeClothes.funFact: Did you know? Matching socks into pairs saves time when you get dressed.
organizeClothes.try: Fold three clothing items and put them in their place. Then say "{name}!"

foldClothesNeatly.about: Folding clothes neatly turns piles into tidy stacks. Neat folds fit in drawers and show care for your clothes.
foldClothesNeatly.funFact: Did you know? Folding clothes when they are cool and dry keeps them from wrinkling.
foldClothesNeatly.try: Fold one shirt or pair of pants carefully. Smooth it and say "{name}!"

arrangeShoes.about: Arranging shoes by the door or on a rack keeps pairs together. Lined-up shoes make leaving home quicker.
arrangeShoes.funFact: Did you know? Shoes left on the floor can cause trips. Putting them in their place keeps everyone safe.
arrangeShoes.try: Pair your shoes and put them in their spot. Then say "{name}!"

keepClassroomClean.about: Keeping the classroom clean means picking up what you drop and not leaving paper on the floor. Clean classes help everyone learn.
keepClassroomClean.funFact: Did you know? A tidy classroom feels proud and welcoming. Every student can help keep it clean.
keepClassroomClean.try: Pick up one piece of litter in class or at your study space. Then say "{name}!"

keepHomeClean.about: Keeping home clean is a team job. Wiping, sweeping, and putting things away keeps the home welcoming.
keepHomeClean.funFact: Did you know? Even two-minute clean-ups after snacks keep kitchens nicer for the next meal.
keepHomeClean.try: Do one small home cleaning task today. Ask what helps most, then say "{name}!"

keepGardenClean.about: Keeping the garden clean means removing litter and not breaking plants. Clean gardens grow better and welcome birds.
keepGardenClean.funFact: Did you know? Plastic trash in gardens can harm soil and animals. Clean soil helps plants grow.
keepGardenClean.try: Remove one piece of trash from a garden or balcony area. Then say "{name}!"

cleanUpAfterPlaying.about: Cleaning up after playing puts the play area back in order. Tidying teaches you to finish what you start.
cleanUpAfterPlaying.funFact: Did you know? Cleanup can be a game. Set a timer or sort toys by color.
cleanUpAfterPlaying.try: After play today, tidy for the length of one song. Then say "{name}!"

wipeSpilledWater.about: Wiping spilled water stops slips and protects floors and books. Quick wipes fix small accidents fast.
wipeSpilledWater.funFact: Did you know? Water on tile can be hard to see and very slippery. A cloth makes floors safe.
wipeSpilledWater.try: If you spill water, wipe it right away with help. When dry, say "{name}!"

recycleWaste.about: Recycling turns clean paper, plastic, or metal into new things. Sorting recyclables helps the Earth.
recycleWaste.funFact: Did you know? An aluminum can can be recycled many times and used again.
recycleWaste.try: Put one clean recyclable in the recycling place. Then say "{name}!"

reuseItems.about: Reusing items means giving jars, boxes, and bags new jobs before throwing them away. Reuse saves useful things.
reuseItems.funFact: Did you know? A clean jar can become a pencil holder. Reusing items reduces waste.
reuseItems.try: Reuse one box or bottle for craft or storage with help. Then say "{name}!"

saveWater.about: Saving water means using only what you need for washing and drinking. Fresh water is precious for people, plants, and animals.
saveWater.funFact: Did you know? Earth has a lot of water, but only a small part is safe to drink. Saving water matters.
saveWater.try: Turn water off while soaping your hands once today. Rinse and say "{name}!"

turnOffTap.about: Turning off the tap when water is not needed stops waste. Closed taps save water drop by drop.
turnOffTap.funFact: Did you know? A dripping tap can waste many buckets of water over a week.
turnOffTap.try: Check that one tap is fully closed after use. Then say "{name}!"

saveElectricity.about: Saving electricity means switching off what you are not using. Using less power helps the planet.
saveElectricity.funFact: Did you know? Much electricity is made using fuel or large machines. Saving a little helps a lot.
saveElectricity.try: Turn off one unused light or device today. Then say "{name}!"

switchOffLights.about: Switching off lights in empty rooms saves power. Daylight through windows can give free light.
switchOffLights.funFact: Did you know? Leaving lights on in sunny rooms wastes electricity.
switchOffLights.try: When you leave a room, turn off the lights. Practice once and say "{name}!"

switchOffFans.about: Switching off fans when you leave saves electricity. Fans cool people, not empty rooms.
switchOffFans.funFact: Did you know? Fans move air on your skin to cool you. They do not store cold air in the room.
switchOffFans.try: Turn off a fan when leaving a room once today. Then say "{name}!"

keepSurroundingsClean.about: Keeping surroundings clean means caring for spaces around you like corridors and building steps. Shared places stay nice when many people help.
keepSurroundingsClean.funFact: Did you know? Clean surroundings invite more play and pride. Mess often leads to more mess.
keepSurroundingsClean.try: Pick up one piece of trash near you and put it in the bin. Then say "{name}!"

doNotLitter.about: Not littering means never throwing wrappers on the ground or out of windows. Litter hurts animals and makes places look bad.
doNotLitter.funFact: Did you know? Animals sometimes eat plastic thinking it is food. Not littering protects them.
doNotLitter.try: Carry a wrapper until you find a bin once today. Then say "{name}!"

plantTrees.about: Planting trees gives shade, cleaner air, and homes for birds. A young tree you water can grow big over many years.
plantTrees.funFact: Did you know? Trees take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen. They help clean the air.
plantTrees.try: Help plant a seed or water a young plant. Then say "{name}!"

waterPlants.about: Watering plants gives roots the water they need to stay green. Regular gentle watering keeps leaves healthy.
waterPlants.funFact: Did you know? Too much water can harm roots. Plants need small amounts of water, not floods.
waterPlants.try: Water one plant carefully with a grown-up. Check the soil and say "{name}!"

feedBirds.about: Feeding birds safely with a grown-up means offering seeds or grains. Kind feeding respects local wildlife.
feedBirds.funFact: Did you know? Different birds like different foods. Mixed grains can attract many birds.
feedBirds.try: With permission, put a little bird food in a safe spot. Watch quietly and say "{name}!"

careForPlants.about: Caring for plants means watering, giving light, and not pulling leaves. Plants are living things that grow with patience.
careForPlants.funFact: Did you know? Checking plant leaves helps you notice when they need water or care.
careForPlants.try: Check one plant: does it need water? Is a leaf dusty? Help it, then say "{name}!"

keepPublicPlacesClean.about: Keeping public places clean means using bins in parks, stations, and markets. Shared places stay pleasant when visitors do not leave trash.
keepPublicPlacesClean.funFact: Did you know? Public places belong to everyone. Cleaning after yourself shows good community manners.
keepPublicPlacesClean.try: In a public place, put your trash in a bin once. Then say "{name}!"

safety.title: Safety Habits
safety.subtitle: Stay safe at home, on the road, and everywhere you go

wearHelmet.about: Wearing a helmet protects your head if you fall on a bike or scooter. Your brain needs this hard shell for safe rides.
wearHelmet.funFact: Did you know? Helmets are tested to absorb crash energy. The strap must be clicked for the helmet to work.
wearHelmet.try: Before a ride, put on a helmet with help. Tap it gently and say "{name}!"

wearSeatBelt.about: A seat belt holds you safely if the car stops suddenly. Buckling up is an important car safety rule.
wearSeatBelt.funFact: Did you know? Seat belts spread crash force so your body stays safer.
wearSeatBelt.try: Buckle up before the car moves. Then say "{name}!"

zebraCrossing.about: Zebra crossings are striped places on the road for walking across safely. Use them when traffic allows.
zebraCrossing.funFact: Did you know? The stripes look like a zebra's pattern. They mark a safe place to cross.
zebraCrossing.try: On a walk, point out a zebra crossing. Name it and say "{name}!"

lookLeftRight.about: Looking left and right before crossing helps you spot cars and bikes. Look with your eyes first, then walk.
lookLeftRight.funFact: Did you know? Traffic can come from both directions. Looking both ways keeps you safe.
lookLeftRight.try: At a safe curb with a grown-up, look left, right, and left again. Then say "{name}!"

holdAdultHand.about: Holding an adult's hand while crossing keeps you safe and guided. Walking together is safer than crossing alone.
holdAdultHand.funFact: Did you know? Cars can see a child and adult together more easily than a child alone.
holdAdultHand.try: Hold a grown-up's hand at the next crossing. Then say "{name}!"

followTrafficSignals.about: Traffic signals tell walkers and drivers when to stop or go. Red means stop. Green means go carefully.
followTrafficSignals.funFact: Did you know? Traffic light colors are the same in many countries. Red for stop is easy to learn.
followTrafficSignals.try: Spot a traffic signal and say what the color means. Then say "{name}!"

stayOnFootpath.about: Staying on the footpath keeps you away from fast vehicles. Sidewalks are made for walking.
stayOnFootpath.funFact: Did you know? Footpaths are shared by walkers and sometimes strollers. Walk carefully and share the space.
stayOnFootpath.try: Walk on the footpath for your next outdoor walk. Then say "{name}!"

doNotRunOnRoad.about: Do not run on the road because cars may not stop in time. Roads are for vehicles; running belongs in parks and playgrounds.
doNotRunOnRoad.funFact: Did you know? Drivers need time to stop. Running on roads is very dangerous.
doNotRunOnRoad.try: Walk calmly near roads today. Then say "{name}!"

doNotPlayOnRoad.about: Roads are not safe for playing. Balls and games belong in yards and playgrounds away from traffic.
doNotPlayOnRoad.funFact: Did you know? A ball rolling onto the road can pull you into danger. Play away from roads.
doNotPlayOnRoad.try: Choose a safe play spot away from vehicles today. Then say "{name}!"

doNotTalkToStrangers.about: Do not go places with strangers or share private information. Saying hello with a grown-up nearby is different from following someone new.
doNotTalkToStrangers.funFact: Did you know? Safe adults ask other grown-ups for help. They do not need secret help from children.
doNotTalkToStrangers.try: Practice saying "No, thank you" and finding your grown-up. Then say "{name}!"

neverGoWithStrangers.about: Never go anywhere with strangers, even if they seem friendly. Only trusted grown-ups should take you places.
neverGoWithStrangers.funFact: Did you know? Even if someone knows your name, always check with your grown-up first.
neverGoWithStrangers.try: Tell a grown-up your safety rule today: never go with strangers. Then say "{name}!"

knowParentsPhone.about: Knowing a parent's phone number helps you reach them if you get separated. Practice the number with a grown-up.
knowParentsPhone.funFact: Did you know? Practicing the number like a song helps you remember it when you feel worried.
knowParentsPhone.try: Practice saying a parent's phone number with a grown-up. Then say "{name}!"

knowHomeAddress.about: Knowing your home address helps helpers find your home if you are lost. Practice saying it clearly.
knowHomeAddress.funFact: Did you know? Saying your area and a nearby landmark with your address helps helpers find you faster.
knowHomeAddress.try: Practice saying your address to a trusted grown-up. Then say "{name}!"

stayWithParentsCrowds.about: In crowds, stay with your parents or grown-up. Hold hands or agree on a meeting spot if you get separated.
stayWithParentsCrowds.funFact: Did you know? Festivals and markets are exciting but easy places to get separated. Stay close to your grown-up.
stayWithParentsCrowds.try: In a busy place, hold a hand or stay in sight of your grown-up. Then say "{name}!"

askPermissionGoing.about: Asking permission before going somewhere lets grown-ups know your plan. This keeps everyone safe and calm.
askPermissionGoing.funFact: Did you know? Telling a grown-up where you are going helps them keep you safe.
askPermissionGoing.try: Ask before leaving for outdoor play once today. Then say "{name}!"

carefulSharpObjects.about: Be careful with scissors, knives, and sharp tools to avoid cuts. Ask grown-ups for help and point blades away from your body.
carefulSharpObjects.funFact: Did you know? Even paper can cut if you are not careful. Use slow, focused hands with sharp things.
carefulSharpObjects.try: When using child scissors, cut slowly while sitting down. Then say "{name}!"

doNotTouchHot.about: Do not touch hot pots, irons, or steam. Hot things can burn your skin. Wait and ask a grown-up for help.
doNotTouchHot.funFact: Did you know? Burns can happen very fast. Metal that looks cool can still be hot inside.
doNotTouchHot.try: From a safe distance, point to one hot item in the kitchen. Learn its name and say "{name}!"

doNotPlayWithFire.about: Do not play with matches, lighters, or candles. Fire can spread quickly and is not a toy for children.
doNotPlayWithFire.funFact: Did you know? Fire can grow faster than you can run. Only grown-ups should use fire tools.
doNotPlayWithFire.try: Tell a grown-up you will not touch fire tools. Then say "{name}!"

stayAwaySockets.about: Stay away from electrical sockets. Do not put fingers, toys, or sticks inside. Electricity is powerful and invisible.
stayAwaySockets.funFact: Did you know? Socket covers exist because outlets are not toys. Keep hands away from them.
stayAwaySockets.try: Look at sockets at home and remember: hands off. Then say "{name}!"

doNotTouchWires.about: Do not touch electric wires, especially broken ones. Tell a grown-up if a wire looks damaged or sparking.
doNotTouchWires.funFact: Did you know? Broken wires are very dangerous. Leave them for adult electricians to fix.
doNotTouchWires.try: If you see a messy wire, tell a grown-up instead of touching it. Then say "{name}!"

carefulNearWater.about: Be careful near pools, buckets, and lakes. Water play needs a grown-up watching and no rough pushing.
carefulNearWater.funFact: Did you know? Young children can slip into even small amounts of water. Empty tubs after use.
carefulNearWater.try: Near water today, stay where a grown-up can see you. Then say "{name}!"

wearLifeJacket.about: A life jacket helps you float if a boat rocks or you get tired in water. Wear one before getting on a boat.
wearLifeJacket.funFact: Did you know? Life jackets help even strong swimmers. Water can surprise anyone.
wearLifeJacket.try: If you go on a boat, wear a life jacket and check straps with help. Then say "{name}!"

keepMedicinesAway.about: Keep medicines away and only take what a grown-up gives you. Pills can look like candy but are not food.
keepMedicinesAway.funFact: Did you know? Medicine amounts are measured carefully. Wrong amounts can hurt instead of help.
keepMedicinesAway.try: Promise to never taste medicine alone. Always ask a grown-up first. Then say "{name}!"

doNotEatUnknown.about: Do not eat unknown berries, powders, or mystery treats. Only eat food from trusted grown-ups and kitchens.
doNotEatUnknown.funFact: Did you know? Some pretty plants are not safe to eat. Colorful does not always mean edible.
doNotEatUnknown.try: If unsure about food, ask before tasting once today. Then say "{name}!"

tellAdultIfSick.about: Tell an adult if you feel sick so you can get rest, water, or care quickly. Saying "I feel sick" is brave and helpful.
tellAdultIfSick.funFact: Did you know? Grown-ups cannot see inside your body. Your words help them know you need help.
tellAdultIfSick.try: Practice saying: "I feel sick." Share if needed and say "{name}!"

callHelpEmergency.about: Calling for help in an emergency means yelling for a grown-up or using emergency numbers with guidance. Fast help can save lives.
callHelpEmergency.funFact: Did you know? Staying as calm as you can helps you speak clearly to helpers.
callHelpEmergency.try: Practice calling a grown-up for help. Speak loudly and clearly, then say "{name}!"

knowEmergencyNumbers.about: Knowing local emergency numbers with a grown-up prepares you for rare scary moments. Use them only for real emergencies.
knowEmergencyNumbers.funFact: Did you know? Emergency lines exist so helpers arrive fast. Joke calls can delay real rescues.
knowEmergencyNumbers.try: Learn one emergency number with a grown-up. Remember the rules and say "{name}!"

followSchoolSafety.about: School safety rules like quiet lines and no pushing on stairs keep many children safe. Following them protects the whole class.
followSchoolSafety.funFact: Did you know? Fire drills feel like practice but train you to stay calm on real emergency days.
followSchoolSafety.try: Name one school safety rule and follow it carefully today. Then say "{name}!"

wearMaskWhenNeeded.about: Wearing a mask when grown-ups say it is needed helps block cough and sneeze droplets. Masks protect you and others.
wearMaskWhenNeeded.funFact: Did you know? Masks work best when they cover both nose and mouth.
wearMaskWhenNeeded.try: Practice putting a mask on correctly if you have one. Adjust it and say "{name}!"

washHandsAfterOutside.about: Washing hands after playing outside removes park dirt and germs. Clean hands keep your food and indoor spaces safer.
washHandsAfterOutside.funFact: Did you know? Outdoor play can leave invisible germs on your hands. Soap removes them.
washHandsAfterOutside.try: After playing outside, wash with soap before snacks. Then say "{name}!"

goodManners.title: Good Manners
goodManners.subtitle: Kind words and gentle actions make everyone feel special

sayHello.about: Saying hello is a friendly greeting. A warm hello helps people feel noticed and starts kind conversations.
sayHello.funFact: Did you know? Hellos look different around the world — waves, namaste, and smiles all mean "I see you."
sayHello.try: Say "Hello!" to someone today with eye contact. Then say "{name}!"

sayGoodMorning.about: Saying good morning greets the new day and the people in it. Morning words spread kindness early.
sayGoodMorning.funFact: Did you know? A cheerful good morning can brighten a sleepy grown-up's day.
sayGoodMorning.try: Tomorrow say "Good morning!" to your family. Then say "{name}!"

sayGoodAfternoon.about: Saying good afternoon is a midday greeting for friends and family. It keeps good manners going after lunch.
sayGoodAfternoon.funFact: Did you know? Afternoon greetings remind us the day still has friendly hours left.
sayGoodAfternoon.try: After lunch, greet someone with "Good afternoon!" Then say "{name}!"

sayGoodEvening.about: Saying good evening welcomes the later part of the day. Evening greetings feel warm as lights turn on.
sayGoodEvening.funFact: Did you know? Evening greetings are common when families reunite after work and school.
sayGoodEvening.try: This evening greet a family member kindly. Then say "{name}!"

sayGoodNight.about: Saying good night closes the day with care. It is a gentle way to say goodbye before sleep.
sayGoodNight.funFact: Did you know? Many families share good-night words and hugs before bed.
sayGoodNight.try: Tonight say "Good night!" to someone you love. Then say "{name}!"

sayGoodbye.about: Saying goodbye shows you notice when someone is leaving. Clear goodbyes help people feel respected.
sayGoodbye.funFact: Did you know? Goodbyes can be words, waves, or both. They mark a kind ending to time together.
sayGoodbye.try: When leaving a place today, say "Goodbye!" Wave and say "{name}!"

sayPlease.about: Saying please turns a request into a polite ask. Please shows you understand others choose to help you.
sayPlease.funFact: Did you know? Please is called a magic word because it often opens doors to help.
sayPlease.try: Ask for something with "please" once today. Then say "{name}!"

sayThankYou.about: Saying thank you shows you notice someone's effort. Grateful words make helpers feel their kindness mattered.
sayThankYou.funFact: Did you know? Thank-yous can be spoken, drawn, or shown with a hug.
sayThankYou.try: Say "Thank you!" for one help you receive today. Then say "{name}!"

saySorry.about: Saying sorry helps when mistakes hurt feelings or bodies. A real sorry means you care and will try to do better.
saySorry.funFact: Did you know? Sorry works best when you also try to fix what went wrong.
saySorry.try: If you bump someone, say "Sorry" and check they are okay. Then say "{name}!"

excuseMe.about: Excuse me politely asks for space, attention, or a path through. It replaces pushing with words.
excuseMe.funFact: Did you know? Excuse me tells people you need to pass or speak. They can make room when they hear it.
excuseMe.try: Say "Excuse me" when passing someone today. Then say "{name}!"

welcome.about: Saying welcome invites someone into your space with warmth. Welcome makes guests feel they belong.
welcome.funFact: Did you know? A welcome smile often comes before welcome words.
welcome.try: Welcome someone to a game or room today. Then say "{name}!"

knockBeforeEntering.about: Knocking before entering respects privacy behind doors. Knocks ask permission instead of surprising people.
knockBeforeEntering.funFact: Did you know? Even a sibling's room deserves a knock. Privacy is an important manners gift.
knockBeforeEntering.try: Knock and wait once before entering a closed room. Then say "{name}!"

askBeforeTaking.about: Asking before taking things shows you respect what belongs to others. Borrowing with permission keeps friendships fair.
askBeforeTaking.funFact: Did you know? Asking "May I use this?" prevents many arguments before they start.
askBeforeTaking.try: Ask before borrowing one item today. Wait for yes, then say "{name}!"

raiseHandSpeaking.about: Raising your hand before speaking in class keeps voices orderly. Teachers can call on you without shouting.
raiseHandSpeaking.funFact: Did you know? Hand-raising is a silent way to say "I have something to share."
raiseHandSpeaking.try: Raise a quiet hand once in a group or pretend class. Then say "{name}!"

waitYourTurn.about: Waiting your turn makes games and lines fair. Everyone gets a chance, including you.
waitYourTurn.funFact: Did you know? Waiting your turn helps you practice self-control, an important life skill.
waitYourTurn.try: In a game or line today, wait calmly for your turn. Then say "{name}!"

listenWhenOthersSpeak.about: Listening when others speak means quiet mouth and open ears. Speakers can finish when listeners wait.
listenWhenOthersSpeak.funFact: Did you know? Good listeners often make the best friends. People feel safe around attentive ears.
listenWhenOthersSpeak.try: Let someone finish a whole sentence before you reply once. Then say "{name}!"

doNotInterrupt.about: Not interrupting means waiting for a pause instead of cutting in. Patience shows respect for speakers.
doNotInterrupt.funFact: Did you know? Interrupting can stop someone from sharing their full idea. Waiting lets ideas finish.
doNotInterrupt.try: Before interrupting once, pause and wait. Then say "{name}!"

speakSoftly.about: Speaking softly indoors keeps spaces calm and ears comfortable. Soft voices fit libraries, nights, and quiet rooms.
speakSoftly.funFact: Did you know? Matching your voice to the place is good manners. Loud voices fit outdoors; soft voices fit indoors.
speakSoftly.try: Use an indoor voice for five minutes at home. Then say "{name}!"

speakPolitely.about: Speaking politely uses kind words and a gentle tone even when you disagree. Polite speech keeps conversations safe for feelings.
speakPolitely.funFact: Did you know? Your tone can change how a sentence feels. Soft tones sound friendlier.
speakPolitely.try: Replace one sharp word with a kinder one today. Then say "{name}!"

respectParents.about: Respecting parents means listening, speaking kindly, and helping when you can. Parents guide and care for you.
respectParents.funFact: Did you know? Respect is not fear. It means treating caregivers with honor while sharing honest feelings.
respectParents.try: Do one helpful thing for a parent without being asked. Then say "{name}!"

respectGrandparents.about: Respecting grandparents means patient listening, gentle hugs, and valuing their stories. Grandparents bring wisdom and family history.
respectGrandparents.funFact: Did you know? Grandparents often know many family stories. Asking questions shows respect.
respectGrandparents.try: Ask a grandparent or elder one story question today. Then say "{name}!"

respectTeachers.about: Respecting teachers means listening, following class rules, and thanking them for lessons. Teachers help your brain grow every day.
respectTeachers.funFact: Did you know? Teachers prepare before you arrive. Respect honors that hard work.
respectTeachers.try: Thank a teacher or learning helper once. Then say "{name}!"

respectElders.about: Respecting elders means polite words, offering seats, and patience. Elders deserve kindness for their long life experience.
respectElders.funFact: Did you know? In many cultures, greeting elders first is an important custom of honor.
respectElders.try: Greet an elder politely today. Offer help if useful and say "{name}!"

respectFriends.about: Respecting friends means sharing fairly, keeping promises, and not teasing to hurt. Friendship grows with mutual respect.
respectFriends.funFact: Did you know? Friends remember how you made them feel more than perfect play skills.
respectFriends.try: Ask a friend what they want to play today. Honor their idea and say "{name}!"

respectEveryone.about: Respecting everyone means kind treatment whether people are like you or different. Every person deserves dignity.
respectEveryone.funFact: Did you know? Respect works everywhere — at home, school, shops, and parks.
respectEveryone.try: Use a polite word with someone new or different today. Then say "{name}!"

shareToys.about: Sharing toys lets more children enjoy playtime. Taking turns keeps toys from causing fights.
shareToys.funFact: Did you know? Sharing does not always mean giving forever. Timed turns still count as sharing.
shareToys.try: Offer a toy turn to someone today. Then say "{name}!"

shareYourFood.about: Sharing food when allowed shows generosity at snack time. Splitting a treat can make two people happy.
shareYourFood.funFact: Did you know? Many festivals celebrate shared meals. Food often tastes better with company.
shareYourFood.try: Share a permitted snack piece with someone today. Then say "{name}!"

helpFriends.about: Helping friends means noticing struggle and offering a hand. Tying a lace or finding a pencil shows you care.
helpFriends.funFact: Did you know? Helping others teaches you to understand how they feel.
helpFriends.try: Help a friend with one small need today. Then say "{name}!"

helpParents.about: Helping parents with small jobs lightens their load and teaches teamwork at home. Helper children grow capable and caring.
helpParents.funFact: Did you know? Parents notice help you give without being asked.
helpParents.try: Carry one item or clear one plate for parents. Then say "{name}!"

helpElderly.about: Helping elderly people might mean carrying a light bag, holding a door, or speaking clearly. Gentle help shows big respect.
helpElderly.funFact: Did you know? Small helps like patient waiting can matter as much as carrying heavy things.
helpElderly.try: Hold a door or offer a seat to an elder once. Then say "{name}!"

beFriendly.about: Being friendly means open smiles and warm invitations to play. Friendly children help others feel less lonely.
beFriendly.funFact: Did you know? One friendly hello can turn a shy day into a brighter one for someone new.
beFriendly.try: Invite someone to play or sit nearby today. Then say "{name}!"

beCaring.about: Being caring means noticing feelings and responding gently. A tissue, a listen, or a check-in shows kindness with attention.
beCaring.funFact: Did you know? Caring for others helps both people feel better.
beCaring.try: Ask "Are you okay?" if someone seems sad. Then say "{name}!"

gentleWithAnimals.about: Being gentle with animals means soft pets and quiet voices. Never pull tails or hurt pets or wild animals.
gentleWithAnimals.funFact: Did you know? Slow, calm moves tell animals you are a friend.
gentleWithAnimals.try: Pet only with permission, using soft strokes from head to back. Then say "{name}!"

congratulateOthers.about: Congratulating others celebrates their wins with joy, not jealousy. Cheering for friends makes success sweeter for everyone.
congratulateOthers.funFact: Did you know? Clapping for others teaches your heart to feel happy for them.
congratulateOthers.try: Congratulate someone for a try or win today. Then say "{name}!"

appreciateOthers.about: Appreciating others means naming what you like about their effort, art, or help. Specific praise feels more real.
appreciateOthers.funFact: Did you know? Saying "I like your careful coloring" feels more meaningful than just "good job."
appreciateOthers.try: Give one specific appreciation today. Then say "{name}!"

acceptMistakes.about: Accepting mistakes means admitting when something went wrong. Mistakes help you learn when you face them honestly.
acceptMistakes.funFact: Did you know? Your brain grows when you pay honest attention to mistakes.
acceptMistakes.try: Admit one small mistake calmly today. Learn from it and say "{name}!"

forgiveOthers.about: Forgiving others releases angry feelings after sorry and time. Forgiveness helps you choose a path toward healing.
forgiveOthers.funFact: Did you know? Forgiveness can help you feel lighter inside.
forgiveOthers.try: If ready, forgive a small mistake today — or ask a grown-up to help talk it out. Then say "{name}!"

keepPromises.about: Keeping promises means doing what you said you would. Reliable words build trust over time.
keepPromises.funFact: Did you know? Small kept promises matter just as much as big ones.
keepPromises.try: Make one small promise you can keep today — and keep it. Then say "{name}!"

useMagicWords.about: Magic words like please, thank you, sorry, and excuse me smooth social situations. Using them often turns talk into kindness.
useMagicWords.funFact: Did you know? They are called magic because moods often change when you use them.
useMagicWords.try: Use three magic words today in real moments. Then say "{name}!"

smileWhileTalking.about: Smiling while talking, when it fits, softens words and welcomes listeners. Friendly faces help shy voices feel braver.
smileWhileTalking.funFact: Did you know? Smiles can be heard in your voice too. Happy tones often come with friendly faces.
smileWhileTalking.try: Say one sentence today with a gentle smile. Then say "{name}!"

environment.title: Environmental Habits
environment.subtitle: Love Earth — trees, water, animals, and clean nature

plantTreesEnv.about: Planting trees gives shade, cleaner air, and homes for birds. Your sapling is a long gift to Earth.
plantTreesEnv.funFact: Did you know? Forests help clean the air. More trees mean more fresh oxygen.
plantTreesEnv.try: Plant a seed or help water a tree sapling. Then say "{name}!"

waterPlantsEnv.about: Watering plants keeps them alive through hot days. Living plants clean air and support insects that birds need.
waterPlantsEnv.funFact: Did you know? Watering in cool morning hours often wastes less water to sun heat.
waterPlantsEnv.try: Water an outdoor or balcony plant carefully once. Then say "{name}!"

savePaper.about: Saving paper means using both sides when you can and not wasting unused sheets. Trees become paper, so using less protects forests.
savePaper.funFact: Did you know? Recycling paper saves trees and reduces trash.
savePaper.try: Use the blank back of one sheet today. Then say "{name}!"

useBothSidesPaper.about: Using both sides of paper makes each sheet last longer. Drafts, doodles, and notes can share one page front and back.
useBothSidesPaper.funFact: Did you know? Notebooks last longer when you write on both sides.
useBothSidesPaper.try: Flip a page and write or draw on the back once. Then say "{name}!"

recyclePlastic.about: Recycling clean plastic keeps bottles from littering land and water. Right bins start the reuse journey.
recyclePlastic.funFact: Did you know? Plastic can last many years in nature. Recycling gives it a second life.
recyclePlastic.try: Rinse and place one plastic bottle in recycling if available. Then say "{name}!"

keepNatureClean.about: Keeping nature clean means leaving parks, beaches, and trails cleaner than you found them. Clean nature stays safe for animals and children.
keepNatureClean.funFact: Did you know? Good explorers take all their trash with them. Nature is not a trash bin.
keepNatureClean.try: Carry litter out of a natural spot once. Then say "{name}!"

protectAnimals.about: Protecting animals means safe habitats, no cruelty, and telling grown-ups about hurt wildlife. Animals share Earth with us.
protectAnimals.funFact: Did you know? Even insects help flowers make fruit. Protecting animals protects food chains.
protectAnimals.try: Do one animal-kind act: put water for birds or do not chase strays. Then say "{name}!"

avoidWastingWater.about: Avoiding water waste means shorter rinses and fixing drips with help. Saved water stays available for drinking and growing food.
avoidWastingWater.funFact: Did you know? A running tap while brushing can waste many glasses of water. Using a cup saves water.
avoidWastingWater.try: Brush teeth with the tap off today. Use a cup to rinse, then say "{name}!"

avoidWastingElectricity.about: Avoiding electricity waste means turning off switches and unplugging idle chargers with help. Saved power helps the Earth.
avoidWastingElectricity.funFact: Did you know? Chargers can use power even with no phone attached. Unplugging unused ones saves energy.
avoidWastingElectricity.try: Unplug one idle charger safely with a grown-up. Then say "{name}!"

school.title: School Habits
school.subtitle: Be a star student with tidy bags and listening ears

reachSchoolOnTime.about: Reaching school on time means less rush and full morning lessons. Being on time shows respect for teachers and your learning.
reachSchoolOnTime.funFact: Did you know? Arriving a little early often feels calmer than arriving at the last second.
reachSchoolOnTime.try: Pack tonight and leave on time tomorrow. Then say "{name}!"

wearCleanUniform.about: A clean uniform shows school pride and keeps you comfortable. Fresh uniforms help mornings feel ready.
wearCleanUniform.funFact: Did you know? Uniforms help students feel like one team. Clean ones keep the team looking neat.
wearCleanUniform.try: Set out a clean uniform tonight. Then say "{name}!"

bringSchoolSupplies.about: Bringing school supplies like pencils, notebooks, and water means you can join every activity. Ready tools make learning smoother.
bringSchoolSupplies.funFact: Did you know? Missing one pencil can slow down a whole worksheet. Spare supplies in your bag help.
bringSchoolSupplies.try: Check pencil, eraser, and notebook tonight. Then say "{name}!"

completeClasswork.about: Completing classwork keeps you with the lesson and shows effort. Finished work helps teachers see what you understand.
completeClasswork.funFact: Did you know? Trying every question is better than leaving blanks. Teachers can help wrong tries, not empty ones.
completeClasswork.try: Finish one class-style task carefully today. Then say "{name}!"

listenToTeacher.about: Listening to the teacher captures instructions and stories that grow your mind. Eyes and ears on the teacher help you learn.
listenToTeacher.funFact: Did you know? Teachers often say key facts only once. Listening carefully helps you catch them.
listenToTeacher.try: Focus your eyes on the speaker for one short talk. Then say "{name}!"

followClassroomRules.about: Classroom rules keep learning fair — quiet voices, kind hands, and walking feet. Rules protect every student's chance to learn.
followClassroomRules.funFact: Did you know? Rules are group promises. When one person breaks them, the whole class is affected.
followClassroomRules.try: Name and follow one classroom rule today. Then say "{name}!"

keepDeskClean.about: A clean desk holds books neatly and leaves space to write. A crumb-free desk helps you concentrate.
keepDeskClean.funFact: Did you know? Erasers often hide on messy desks. A clean desktop saves search time.
keepDeskClean.try: Clear your desk or study spot of trash once. Then say "{name}!"

respectSchoolProperty.about: Respecting school property means not breaking walls, books, or benches. Shared tools stay nice for next year's students too.
respectSchoolProperty.funFact: Did you know? School things belong to the whole community. Treating them well is good citizenship.
respectSchoolProperty.try: Handle one school or home learning tool gently today. Then say "{name}!"

returnBorrowedBooks.about: Returning borrowed books on time lets other readers enjoy them. Library manners keep story doors open for everyone.
returnBorrowedBooks.funFact: Did you know? Late books delay someone else's reading. Returning on time is a form of sharing.
returnBorrowedBooks.try: Find a borrowed book and plan its return date. Then say "{name}!"

helpClassmates.about: Helping classmates means explaining kindly, sharing pencils, or welcoming new students. Classrooms shine when children support each other.
helpClassmates.funFact: Did you know? Teaching a classmate a small tip helps you remember it better too.
helpClassmates.try: Help a classmate or sibling learner once today. Then say "{name}!"
